Containment & Termination Protocol: These things are large-scale destroyers.  The inhabitants of Tartarus Colony lured the creatures to the surface and attacked them with aircraft with limited success before the beasts learned to avoid such traps.  The best way to kill a rampaging Harvester is to attack its soft, unprotected underbelly – but good luck getting close enough to do so without being crushed or ground up.

Lion Worms

An aggressive carnivore covered in golden, fast-moving cilia, the Lion Worm is the apex predator on the xenobiologist jungle dreamworld of Zagreus.  Eyeless, the Lion Worm instead has a series of ears running along its body with a group of nostrils in the center of its huge, razor-sharp beak.  Like the Harvesters of Tartarus, the worm is a burrower, but unlike those giant land animals, the Lion Worm can only travel through soft earth.  It is an ambush predator that actively seeks live prey.  It’s rumored that poachers have been removing Lion Worms from their natural habitat, slipping them past ICC quarantine and selling them to the corporate elite as pets.  If this is so, it is a potential disaster waiting to happen – an escaped Lion Worm could reproduce quickly and upset the ecological balance of any colony world, as well as be responsible for a great many deaths.

LION WORM
> Type Invertebrate Carnivore
> Habitat Wilds of Zagreus
> Size 1.8–3 meters
> Traits Relentless hunter, attacks first, retreats underground when confused
Speed 2
Health 8
Skills 8
Mobility MOBILITY 10, OBSERVATION 8
Armor Level 1

Containment & Termination Protocol: Lion Worms can be disoriented by the release of pollen or pollutants in the air.  They are easily distracted by the pheromones of another Lion Worm, something the colonists on Zagreus were wise enough to collect.  A Lion Worm perceives the smell of another of its kind as an invasion of its hunting grounds and will seek out and attack the offender accordingly.

HUMAN’S BEST FRIEND

When humanity conquers a brave new world, they bring their animal companions with them – and with good reason.  Pets are incredibly important to the psychological well-being of long-haul starship crews, and every ship should have one.  While far from common, typical flesh and blood animals found on the Frontier include dogs, cats, mice, reptiles, fish, and birds.  Additionally, synthetic copies of both mundane and exotic Earth animals have been produced by a number of companies.  Rats and insects have stowed away on many a spacecraft, spreading disease and altering the ecology of alien worlds. Apes are still used in laboratory settings and cattle, sheep, horses, and pigs have all been transplanted to extrasolar farming colonies.

Ambush Predator: The Lion Worm is a top predator.  In its own territory it will set up traps, pits, walls of vines, and tree lines that all help it capture its prey.  In stealth mode, a Lion Worm’s prey gets −2 dice to OBSERVATION rolls due to the Worm’s cunning instincts, if they are in the Lion Worm’s territory.

D6   ATTACK
1   Intimidating Display: The Lion Worm rears up, its golden cilia flowing in threatening patterns.  But it’s a bluff.  The expert predator has seen a problem and is using an aggressive display to cover a tactical retreat.  All PCs within Short range must make a panic roll. On its next turn, the Lion Worm attempts to leave combat (Leaving Combat ) and stealth mode resumes.  When it makes its next attack, it gets a +1 to its roll on this table (to a maximum of 6).
2   Playing With Its Prey. The Lion Worm attacks but for fun, rather than to kill.  Roll for the attack with eight base dice. If the attack hits, the target drops a weapon (or other item) of the GM*s choice, but is otherwise unharmed.  The Worm rears over them, wishing for its prey to run before it attacks again.  The victim must make an immediate panic roll.
3   Acrid Pheromones. The Lion Worm releases a huge dump of pheromones into the air.  They are so pungent that anyone near the creature starts to cough, and all PCs within Short range must make a STAMINA roll (no action) or lose their next turn.
4   Feral Rage. The beast attacks, throwing everything at its victim, with ten base dice, base damage 2.  If it causes any damage, its insatiable desire to kill allows it to immediately make a second attack, with the same effect.
5   Crippling Attack. The Lion Worm attacks to incapacitate its target, either to eat later or get enough space to escape a bad situation.  It goes for a crippling blow, making an attack with eight base dice, base damage 1, armor piercing.  If it does any damage, the victim is automatically broken.
6   Death Roll. The Lion Worm goes full out for the kill, grasping its target and wrapping it in a vicious death roll.  Roll for the attack with ten base dice, base damage 1, armor piercing.  If the attack hits, the victim is grappled (Grappling ) and must win an opposed roll for CLOSE COMBAT against the Lion Worm’s MOBILITY to break loose.  On its next turn, the Lion Worm squeezes the victim, attacking with ten Base Dice, base damage 1 again.  This continues until the victim is killed or breaks free.

Tanakan Scorpionids

Although they are equipped with poisonous stingers, the desert scorpions of Tanaka 5 have more in common with Earth’s prehistoric sea scorpions than the standard Terran variety.  These tapered and segmented creatures have rounded heads, a set of large pincers, eight crab-like legs, and two large fin-like structures on either side of their bodies.  While initially thought to be utilized in intimidation displays, the fins were found to have a different purpose when the planet’s underground lake systems were discovered – Scorpionids are adept swimmers and spend at least half their life underwater.  Those very lakes are teeming with aquatic life, making for easy hunting grounds for the arthropods.

“What kind of bio-stock did these bugs punch out of?”
Cpl.  Dwayne Hicks  
SCORPIONID
> Type Arthropod Carnivore
> Habitat Tanaka 5, deserts and cavernous springs
> Size 1.5–2.4 meters
> Traits Hides in dunes and rocks during the day, hunts at night, aggressive if provoked and surprisingly adept swimmers.
  ON LAND IN WATER
Speed 1 3
Health 5 5
Mobility 6 10
OBSERVATION 6 10
Armor Level 1 (0 Vs firearms) 1 (0 Vs firearms)

While they normally keep to themselves, Scorpionids will fight if they feel threatened.  Their pincers can break a man’s leg, and their sting can kill a grown human quickly unless an antidote is administered.  The deadly venom in their stingers can be used for a multitude of medicinal purposes.  While dangerous and somewhat unpleasant, collecting Scorpionids and milking their venom can make you some quick cash.  Scorpionids run a gamut of colors from an orange-red to a deep blue.

D6   ATTACK
1   Retreat. The Scorpionid isn’t stupid and won’t fight unless there’s a good reason to.  On this occasion it decides to flee the fight (Leaving Combat) as quickly as possible.
2   Pinned Down. The Scorpionid uses its powerful pincers to pin down its target.  Roll for the attack using ten base dice, base damage 1.  If the attack hits, the target drops a weapon (or other item) and must make an immediate panic roll.
3   Pincer Grab. The creature tries to seize its victim in its enormous claws, quivering with the anticipation of a quick strike with its huge tail.  Roll for the attack with eight base dice, base damage 1.  If the attack hits, the victim is grappled (Grappling ) and must win an opposed roll for CLOSE COMBAT against the Scorpionid’s MOBILITY to break loose.  If the Scorpionid retains its grasp, it will automatically make a Tail Strike attack against the victim on its next turn.  If this attack hits underwater, the Scorpionid will also drag the victim deeper and one zone away from the group, causing them to also suffer the effects of drowning.
4   Flailing Strike. The Scorpionid’s pincer swipes at its target.  Roll for the attack with eight base dice, base damage 1.  If the attack hits, the Scorpionid flings the victim into the next zone, causing another point of damage.
5   Tail Strike. The Scorpionid swings its terrible tail forward with deadly purpose.  It attacks with ten base dice, base damage 1, armor piercing.  If it inflicts any damage, it also poisons the victim with a deadly venom, counting as a disease with a virulence rating of –2 (Disease ).
6   Immobilize. The Scorpionid wants to escape, but to do so it needs to take its attackers out of the fight.  It lunges for its victim’s legs with its huge claws, making an attack with eight base dice, base damage 2.  If it does any damage, the victim immediately suffers an Impaled Thigh critical injury (Critical Injuries ) even if not broken.

Underwater Sprint: If starting its turn in water, when a Scorpionid moves instead of performing a signature attack (below), it can move an additional zone.  It uses this ability to make sneak attacks against prey on the shore.  

Containment & Termination Protocol: Their shells protect them from knives and other melee weapons but don’t do much good against bullets.

The Swarm

Dubbed space locusts by Colonial Marines, the Swarm either originated on or came to rest on planet LV-KR 115.  For untold centuries, they would ravage the grasslands for a season before going into hibernation for decades, only awakening when the lands were fertile once again.  Between cycles, the company discovered the world and devised a method for creating self-replenishing crops there.

D6   ATTACK
1   Consume. The Swarm consumes everything in its path, and this place is rich in food.  The Swarm’s Health is restored by 2 points, making it harder to drive off.
2   Pheromones. The Swarm is getting increasingly agitated and more and more pheromones are being released into the air.  The Swarm’s next roll on this table gets +1.
3   Suffocating Swarm. The swarming creatures are everywhere.  They are in the victims’ eyes, ears and mouths, and it is almost impossible to breathe.  Everyone inside the Swarm area must make a STAMINA roll.  Failure means the victim loses their next turn, and the Swarm will perform a Stripped To The Bone attack against one victim on its next turn.
4   Desperate Hunger. The Swarm is so hungry it will eat anything, and right now the polymers and compounds in the players’ armor look good.  Everyone within the Swarm wearing armor suffers an attack rolled with eight base dice, base damage 1.  Any damage is immediately subtracted from the armor level.  Those not wearing armor find their clothes have been shredded, but the attack does not inflict any damage.
5   Feeding Frenzy. The Swarm is hungry and tries to eat anything it can envelope.  All characters inside the Swarm suffer an attack rolled with six base dice, base damage 1, armor piercing (as the creatures look for ways to slip past it).
6   Stripped To The Bone. The Swarm focuses on one target, and that victim takes an attack rolled with twelve base dice, base damage 1, armor piercing.  If the attack inflicts any damage, the Swarm will automatically attack the target again on its next turn.  This will continue until an attack fails to inflict damage, the victim is stripped to the bone, rescued, or the Swarm is driven off.

The swarm awoke once more to devour everything.  But with crops that could grow back after any attack, the swarm had no reason to go into hibernation.  Instead, their numbers grew exponentially until they blanketed the entire planet.  The company was forced to bomb the planet with pesticides that rendered the planet uninhabitable.

While severe in its solution, the problem was solved for LV-KR 115, but that was only the beginning.  The term space locust seems to have been apt, as scientists have drawn a line across the Frontier of worlds that have suffered repeated ecological blights, and dormant swarms have been located adrift in deep space.  It is possible that these insects drift in space for millennia before reaching new worlds to ravage.  No one knows how many are out there, nor how many already lay dormant on fertile colony worlds, just waiting to wake up and begin the cycle again.

Swarm Rules: The size of a Swarm is measured in the number of zones it covers.  The Speed rating of a Swarm is equal to the number of zones it covers.  The Health of a Swarm is equal to 5 times the number of zones it covers.  The Swarm cannot be killed.  Victims can only flee from it or try to drive it off.  If the Swarm’s Health drops to zero it has had enough and goes looking for easier pickings.  

Containment & Termination Protocol: Good luck.  Try shooting them all you want, there are hundreds to take the place of every locust you might hit.  In space, you can cook the dormant critters in your afterburners.  Once planetside, fire, electrical conductivity, and lethal pesticides are the only means to deal with this spaceborne environmental menace.

THE SWARM
> Type Insect Omnivores
> Habitat LV-KR 115, fertile grass and farmlands, or drifting through space
> Size Around 15 centimeters each, but together they can form massive swarms a great many kilometers in diameter
> Traits Swarm an area, consume everything there save for metals
Speed 1 per zone
Health 5 per zone
Armor Level Impervious to all attacks except fire, explosions, and electricity.

11. CAMPAIGN PLAY.name: 11. CAMPAIGN  PLAY
11. CAMPAIGN PLAY.text:
WHAT DO THE PLAYER CHARACTERS DO? WHERE DO THEY GO? Just what is out there? This chapter provides the tools to help you as the GM develop a framework for creating a campaign as well as colony worlds and other adventure destinations.  It provides random tables that are bursting with ideas for missions, complications, encounters and more, whether your players are space truckers, colonial marines or frontier colonists.

Bear in mind that random rolls are an aid to imagination and that you can always simply pick an entry from one of the tables if you prefer.

THE CAMPAIGN FRAME

BEFORE YOU SET OUT to play a full campaign in the ALIEN roleplaying game, you need to decide which campaign frame to play – simply put, who the characters are and what role they have in the ALIEN universe.  This is something we recommend that you do together with the players, as you will have more fun if everyone is involved in creating the game.  

Three suggested campaign frames – space truckers, colonial marines, and frontier colonists – are described below, and later in this chapter you’ll find mission generators for each of them.

Whichever campaign frame you choose, you should decide early on if the PCs are employed by a government, a corporation or the military, or if they are freelancers, taking whatever jobs they can find in their field.

As employees, the PCs get a steady paycheck (even though it might be a small one) and access to hardware that most freelancers cannot afford.  Freelancers have a lot less security, but they are free to take whatever jobs they like, and if they’re lucky they might one day strike it big.

Where To Start

You can start your campaign anywhere you like in charted space (see chapter 8 ), but such a wide freedom of choice can be daunting.  At the end of this chapter, you’ll find three campaign locations that are described in some detail and can function as a starting point or even a home base for the PCs: the Tartarus Sector, the Jackson’s Star mining colony, and the Novgorod space station.

Starting Spaceship

We recommend that you let the players start with access to a spaceship.  This way they are mobile right from the start and can explore the star map and discover the ALIEN universe piece by piece.  Space travel is explained in detail in chapter 6 .

If the PCs are employed by a government, corporation or the military, their spaceship will be assigned to them, and they are expected to take good care of it.  If the PCs are freelancers, they can lease or even own their own spaceship, and use money they earn to repair and upgrade it.  This can turn into a mini game on its own – read more in chapter 6 .

Space Truckers

You don’t give a damn about the colonies.  You’ve got bills to pay – and the easy money is in hauling cargo and refineries from the Outer Rim to the Core Worlds.  While there is plenty of difficult and frustrating work at both ends of the trip, most of the job is spent in hypersleep, traveling from here to there while the ship flies itself.  Thanks to the cryo-chambers, you’re aging a lot slower than your buddies back home.  Keep on truckin’ and you just might live forever.  If you’re lucky, you’ll be home in time to see your newborn’s third birthday.  Until then, you’ve got to convince the Company that your work on this stint is worth a full share.

As the crew of a powerful tug-ship or cargo hauler, the PCs will be employees of the ship’s owner and their jobs will vary tremendously depending on the client’s needs.  They may be ferrying ore to a refinery or taking colonists in hypersleep out to an unexplored planet.  There are supplies to ferry to colonies, drilling rigs to tow out to the frontier and salvage jobs to carry out.  Have ship – will travel.

The tables later in this chapter suggest some of the common cargoes to ship and the possible destinations for delivery.  Although sounding mundane, this job is filled with problems, complications, and unexpected encounters with the unknown.  You are on your own, often navigating on the fringes of known space … breakdowns, emergencies and the frustrations of working with two-bit colonies can be turned into enjoyable scenarios in themselves.

  • Typical Jobs: Cargo Runs
  • Suggested Employers: Weyland-Yutani, Lasalle Bionational, Seegson
  • Suggested Careers: Company Agent, Medic, Officer, Pilot, Roughneck
  • Suggested Spaceship: MODEL CM-88G BISON M-Class Commercial Starfreighter
  • Weekly Salary: $400–960 (time in stasis pays 10%)

Colonial Marines

Most of your friends will never see another world… but not you.  As soon as you were old enough, you signed up for the USCMC.  The pay is poor and the food is worse but you’ve always got a bunk and you get to shoot all kinds of weaponry at all kinds of targets.  Life in the Corps is never dull, it’s one gigantic adrenaline rush – but the luster has begun to fade.  You’ve seen things that you’ll never be able to forget – and plenty that you wish you could.

The life of a colonial marine can be tough and challenging, particularly when it comes to the missions.  There is no employer table for marines, all their orders come from the Marine Corps HQ.  The missions are typically combat orientated with military objectives, but you can substitute tables from the other campaign frame for inspiration if desired.  Most mission locations will involve off-world installations, war zones, combat stations or fortifications.  The key to playing a Colonial Marine game is to have the PCs be the squad leaders, those making all of the decisions.  Also, keep the squad small.  This is a roleplaying game, after all, not a wargame.

  • Typical Jobs: Military Missions
  • Suggested Employers: USCMC (United Americas), Space Operating Forces (Union of Progressive Peoples), Royal Marines Commandos (Three World Empire)
  • Suggested Careers: Colonial Marine, Medic, Officer, Pilot, Roughneck
  • Suggested Spaceship: CONESTOGA-CLASS FRIGATE
  • Weekly Salary: $500–760 (time in stasis pays 10%)

Frontier Colonists

CHAIN OF COMMAND

Marines, regardless of whether they work for the UA, 3WE or the UPP, are part of a military organization and are expected to follow orders.  This means that the PCs don’t get to choose which missions they are sent on, someone higher up simply gives them orders.  In game terms, this means that you as GM prepare a mission and give the players a briefing on the objectives.  If you want a more open approach, we recommend the PCs being a mercenary company instead.  This way, they are free to choose where to go and which missions they want to take on.

“Hey, Hicks.  Man, you look just like I feel.”
Private Drake  

“Life on the off-world colonies is an adventure,” they said.  “Start a new life with the prospect for untold riches,” they said.  What they didn’t say was that the colony worlds are tough and unforgiving, and while opportunities for making a fortune do exist, it always seems to happen to the other guy.  But your chance will come – you are a surveyor, a prospector, a miner and an explorer – and if there are treasures out here, you will find them.  And then you can sell your claim to one of the corporations for a fortune.”

Frontier colonists are blue-collar working stiffs, and they follow up rumors, take chances on speculation or simply go in blind, to locate and extract valuable raw materials or salvage abandoned technology.  Their skills and tenacity are sought after by third parties not willing to brave the dangers of the Outer Rim themselves.  Finding the big bucks to fund your own expedition is not easy.  This makes most explorers dependent on sponsors.  The rewards are often permits to go on expeditions of one’s own, or new, desirable knowledge.

  • Typical Jobs: Expeditions
  • Suggested Employers: Weyland-Yutani, ICSC, Colonial Marshal Bureau
  • Suggested Careers: Colonial Marshal, Company Agent, Kid, Medic, Pilot, Roughneck, Scientist
  • Suggested Spaceship: MODEL CM-90S CORVUS G-Class Commercial Deep Space Salvage Vessel
  • Weekly Salary: $500–640 (time in stasis pays 10%)

CREATING STAR SYSTEMS

THE RULES IN THIS SECTION allow you to create a colony world on the Frontier or Outer Rim and with it all the information you need to start running scenarios with your players.  Should the wider star system require further exploration, then optional rules are included to create all the planets around a star

Stars vary wildly from moon-sized white dwarfs to immense giants and from dull red, cool M-types, to fierce white and blue stars.  A star type is described by combining its brightness class and its spectral class, for example: MV, GIII, FV.  There are no stars of brightness class type I and II within charted space.

TYPE DESCRIPTION BRIGHTNESS CLASS
Giant Huge, bright and cool star in a late stage of evolution Type III
Subgiant A large, bright star, exhausting its fuel Type IV
Main Sequence Small but incredibly common type of star Type V
White Dwarf A dead, burnt-out star, tiny and super-dense Type DA
Red Dwarf A red main sequence star, small and cool.  Very common star. Type MV
White Main Sequence White main sequence stars that burn hot and brightly Type AOV

Class: Stars are also given a spectral class, based on temperature.  These are:
 
  • O – Blue
  • B – Blue
  • A – White
  • F – Yellow-White
  
  • G – Yellow
  • K – Orange
  • M – Red
  

PLANETARY NAMES

Inhabited planets are given names that often refer to Greek mythology, or to dark or foreboding themes.  Unsurveyed planets and moons remain unnamed, while any surveyed moon or planet (prior to colonization) will be given a three-digit designation prefixed by the ICC code “LV” (for example LV-562). A suggested list of names is provided here:

  • Hannibal
  • Monos
  • Requiem
  • Nakaya
  • Phaeton
  • Nocturne
  • Prospero
  • Magdala
  • Hamilton
  • Tracatus
  • Aurora
  • Hephaestus
  • Damnation
  • Cerberus
  • Doramin
  • Solitude
  • Euphrates
  • Nemesis
  • Moab
  • Gorgon
  • Napier
  • Medea

Main World Creation

Human presence in a star system will be established on the most lucrative planet, not the most Earth-like.  It might have poisonous air and seas of sulfuric acid, but if there’s palladium or iridium to mine, then that’s where the colony will go.  This colonized world will sometimes be referred to as the main world, to differentiate it from all of the uninhabited planets and moons in the rest of the star system.

Each main world requires you to randomly create its size, atmosphere, temperature and geosphere.  One random planetary feature can then be created (to give an initial impression of the world’s surface) before moving on to the colony size, colony mission, factions at work and any orbital components.

Planet Size

The size listed is the diameter of the planet in kilometers, with examples of roughly equivalent bodies from our solar system.  Worlds with lower than 0.7 G are considered low-gravity worlds while those of 1.3 G or above are classed as high gravity.  On both low and high-G worlds, characters will have trouble moving around and get a –2 modification to all AGILITY, CLOSE COMBAT and STAMINA rolls.  After a period of acclimation, this modification disappears.

  2D6   SIZE SURFACE GRAVITY EXAMPLES
  2 or less   <1,000 km Almost 0-G Ceres and other asteroids
  3-4   2,000 km 0.1G Iapetus
  5-6   4,000 km 0.2G Luna, Europa
  7   7,000 km 0.5G Mars
  8   10,000 km 0.7G
  9-10   12,500 km 1.0G Earth, Venus
  11   15,000 km 1.3G
  12   20,000 km 2G Super-Earth

Use the below modifier if applicable (see Star System Generator ):

  • Ice planet –2
  • Gas giant moon –4

Atmosphere

The size of a planet may affect the atmosphere, with the low-digit entries (2–8) generally more common for small worlds and the higher ones (9–12) associated with larger worlds.  Many planets have toxic and unbreathable atmospheres.

> Thin: In a very thin atmosphere, a pressure suit is needed.  Without it, all STAMINA rolls get –2 dice and all PCs must make a fatigue roll every shift.  On some worlds with a thin atmosphere, deep ravines can contain pressure high enough for humans to survive without suits.  

> Breathable: The atmosphere is at Earth density and contains oxygen and carbon dioxide in quantities to sustain human life.

  2D6   ATMOSPHERE
  3 or less   Thin
  4-6   Breathable
  7-8   Toxic
  9   Dense
  10   Corrosive
  11   Infiltrating
  12   Special
Modify the roll for planet size:
  • 4,000 km diameter or less: –6
  • 4,001 km – 7,000 km diameter: –2

> Toxic: The toxic atmosphere has an Earth-like density, but it is not breathable without a filter mask.  Anyone without a mask must make a fatigue roll every stretch (in combat, the fatigue roll does not count as an action).  

> Dense: The air is so dense that it is literally too thick to breathe.  Only at high altitudes can humans breathe comfortably without a pressure suit.  Exposure can lead to reduced blood circulation, resulting in numbness, cramps and even life-threatening clots.  Without a pressure suit, all PCs must make a fatigue roll every shift.  

> Corrosive: Corrosive atmospheres are toxic and contain chemicals such as ammonia, fluorine or chlorine that burns the throat and lungs.  These count as toxic (above) but in addition, anyone without a pressure suit suffers an attack rolled with five base dice at the start of each stretch.  Normal armor has no scol3ect.  

> Infiltrating: Corrosive gases in great concentration can defeat pressure suits.  This type of atmosphere is classed as infiltrating.  It has the same scol3ect as corrosive above, but roll for an attack with five base dice against each pressure suit.  On a hit, the suit is breached and no longer offers any protection.  

> Special: The atmosphere varies across the planet’s surface.  It could be dense at the equator and thin around the poles, have a liquid form or some other special properties decided by you.  If stuck for ideas, re-roll.

Temperature

The average surface temperature of a planet depends on its distance from the star as well as the planet’s atmosphere.  This temperature provides a clue as to its position in the star system.

  2D6   TEMPERATURE AVERAGE TEMPERATURE DESCRIPTION
  3 or less   Frozen –50°C or less Titan, Pluto, Enceladus
  4-5   Cold –50 to 0°C Alaska or Antarctica in winter
  6-7   Temperate 0 to 30°C Boston or Paris
  8-10   Hot 31 to 80°C Mojave or Sahara Deserts
  11+   Burning 80°C or more Mercury, Venus
Add or subtract the modifiers listed below, if applicable:
  • Thin atmosphere: –4
  • Dense atmosphere: -1
  • Corrosive or infiltrating atmosphere: +6
  • Special atmosphere: GM decides
“You hear that?”
“What?”
“Nothing.  No birds, no animals.  Nothing.”
Daniels and Oram  

Geosphere

Results on the table below tell you the proportion of dry land to ocean that exists on the planet.  Note that a frozen world will have locked up all of the seas and oceans as ice and a Burning world will have turned its oceans to steam.  Also, it should be pointed out that, when it comes to other planets, not all oceans are comprised of water.

  2D6   GEOSPHERE DESCRIPTION
  4 or less   Desert World No surface water
  5-6   Arid World Global deserts and dry steppes, with some lakes and small seas
  7-8   Temperate-Dry World Oceans cover 30–40% of the world’s surface
  9-10   Temperate-Wet World Oceans cover 60–70% of the world’s surface
  11   Wet World Global oceans with some islands and archipelagos
  12   Water World No dry land
Modify the roll for the factors below:
  • Thin, dense, corrosive or infiltrating atmosphere: –4
  • Special atmosphere: GM decides
  • Hot temperature: –2
  • Burning temperature: –4
  • Frozen –2
  • No atmosphere = Desert World

Terrestrial Planet Terrain

Roll on this table for a single distinctive planetary terrain type.  If using the star system generator (Star System Generator ) these results are only suitable for terrestrial planets – for ice planets, use the ice planet terrain table instead.

 
D66   FEATURE
≤ 11   Huge impact crater
12   Plains of silicon glass
13   Disturbing wind-cut rock formations
14   Permanent global dust-storm
15   Eerily colored dust plains
16   Active volcanic lava fields
21   Extensive salt flats
22   Dust-laden, permanent sunset sky
23   Ancient, blackened lava plains
24   Thermal springs and steam vents
25   Tall, gravel-strewn mountains
26   Howling winds that never stop
31   Daily fog banks roll in
32   Deep and wide rift valleys
33   Bizarrely eroded, wind-cut badlands
34   Steep-sided river gorges cut into soft rocks
35   Huge moon dominates day/night sky
36   World-spanning super canyon
 
D66   FEATURE
41   Impressive river of great length
42   Oddly colored forests of alien vegetation
43   Mountains cut by sky-blue lakes
44   Sweeping plains of elephant grass
45   Highly toxic, but beautiful, plant-life
46   Small, bright, incredibly fast moons in orbit
51   Vast and complex river delta
52   Immense series of waterfalls
53   Endless mudflats with twisting waterways
54   Impressive coastline of fjords and cliffs
55   Volcanoes, active & widespread
56   Impenetrable jungle
61   Dangerous tides—fast and loud
62   Vast, permanent super storm
63   Toxic sea creatures floating with the currents
64   Volcanic island chains
65   Permanently overcast with unrelenting rainfall
≥ 66   Mildly acidic oceans and rainfall
 
2D6   FEATURE
2   Huge impact crater
3   Geysers spew water into low orbit from long fissures
4   Deep fissures leading to a subsurface ocean
5   Dramatically colored blue-green ice fissures
6   Huge and active cryovolcano

JOB GENERATOR

THIS CHAPTER PROVIDES YOU with tools and inspiration for quick creation of jobs and missions for your players.  First, roll up the basics for the job using the guidelines below.  Then, use the tables for each individual campaign frame to add the details.

> System: Roll D6–1 to determine the distance to the destination system.  Pick a system on the star map on the inside covers of this book (or in the Hope’s Last Day Starter Set) at this distance from the PCs’ current location.  On a result of zero, the destination is in the same star system

> Difficulty: Roll a D3 to determine the general difficulty of the job – a 1 indicates a routine mission while a 3 indicates something difficult and out of the ordinary.  The difficulty will determine the number of complications during the job

> Payment: To determine the base payment offered for the job, add the two results above (getting a total sum from 1 to 8).  Multiply the sum by the number of PCs, and then by $1,000.  With a successful MANIPULATION roll, the PCs can negotiate to increase the payment by 20% per    rolled, or instead spend    to gain some bonus reward.

ENCOUNTERS

ADVENTURE, DANGER AND HORROR sit beyond the comforts of Earth, out in the off-world colonies, in the depths of space and on unexplored worlds.  Travel by starship through hyperspace to reach these destinations will bring the PCs into contact with other ships, hazards and problems.  

The tables on the following pages should only be used if doing so adds something to the game.  You are completely free to ignore them and let the journey be problem-free, or simply skip the traveling and open the scenario as the group arrives at its destination.

SHORE LEAVE

DURING CAMPAIGN PLAY, life doesn’t just come to a stop when the PCs arrive at a colony or space station following a mission.  The players may want to enjoy their shore leave in-character, roleplaying some of their downtime away from life-or-death situations and constant stress.  This interlude allows PCs to recover, to show a new side of their personality, and pursue their personal agendas.

For each week of shore leave, each PC selects one of the following activities:

  • die: A PC with one or more critical injuries will need time to die (Critical Injuries ).
  • Recover: A PC who has suffered Mental Trauma may attempt to recover by resting, soul-searching, seeking counseling, or something else.  Make a roll for Empathy.  It cannot be pushed.  If successful, one mental trauma is removed.
  • Pursue Agenda: A PC may pursue their Personal Agenda in some way.  This can be roleplayed, but keep it short to avoid keeping other players waiting.  If the agenda is successfully pursued, the PC gains one XP.
  • Socialize: PCs who don’t need or want to do any of the above may instead socialize with the locals.  Roll once on the appropriate table for shore leave events.

Expenses: During shore leave, the PCs must pay their way.  For typical weekly living expenses, see Living Expenses.

TARTARUS SECTOR

“Hell, there are no rules out here – this is Tartarus!”
Alessandro de Sosa, Warden of Skyfire Down Corrections Facility, LV-2412  

WELCOME TO TARTARUS SECTOR. This area in the Outer Rim Territories, briefly described in chapter 9 , is expanded here as a possible campaign setting for the game.  With twelve planetary systems described in detail, and a summary of what’s going down across the sector, here you will find everything you need to run any style of campaign in the frontier sector of Tartarus.  Your player group – of space truckers, colonists, explorers, corporates, or colonial marines – will find all the challenge, excitement, and horror they can take.

Brief History

Tartarus sector occupies the rimward-trailward frontier of human settlement, beyond which lies unexplored space.  Riven with conflict, its name – the infernal realm of torment of Greek mythology – is an apt description.

The United Americas (UA) has dominated Tartarus sector since it established Torin Prime in 2104, but that dominance is fragile.  The sector is unruly, and the UA’s military strength is thin and low on supplies.  They rely on the Outer Rim Defense Fleet (ORDF), a ragtag militia of UA colonists in uniform.  Their main challenge comes from the Three World Empire (3WE), but civil unrest within the 3WE’s sphere of influence saw Colonial Marines step in as peacekeepers, but they never give the colonies back.  The two superpowers have locked horns across the sector ever since.

Of the others, the Union of Progressive Peoples (UPP) shows the greatest interest in Tartarus.  scol3orts to support rebel factions, or those seeking independence, while quietly colonizing across the sector, are the extent of the UPP’s ambitions thus far – but that is about to change.

With this volatile mix, some fear the Frontier War will come to Tartarus.  In an attempt to bring calm, the Independent Core System Colonies (ICSC) established Argos colony, a commercial and political hub, and neutral ground.  Deliberately kept separate from the new Anchorpoint station located just beyond the Tartarus Rimward boundary, Argos colony is a place to resolve disputes and keep the peace, while Anchorpoint is the waystation to the Far Reach and deep space.

Life for the average Joe is tough.  Food is shit, the worlds are grim, and the wages...  With the threat of conflict, it’s a wonder any make Tartarus home at all.  Unfortunately for most who live there, they don’t have any other choice.  But despite the hardships, Tartarus is awash with opportunities.

Systems & Colonies

Ross 619 – Skyfire Down

Skyfire Down is a penal colony, controlled by Warden Alessandro de Sosa, a Lunnar-Welsun executive.  Protected by the USCMC, the planet is also home to a naval shipyard.  It’s a grim place, with radiation zones and industrial waste littering the landscape, illuminated by the perpetual display of meteors falling from a ring of orbital junk.

Inmates work in LV-2412’s mines and shipyard, and off-world, on projects that need a disposable workforce.  Escape attempts are common.

Five years ago, the 3WE shipped thousands of convicts to Skyfire Down, when their detention center on Fiori 16 was decommissioned.  Within these ranks they hid a crack unit of Royal Marines with one mission – win over Skyfire Down’s convicts and lead a prison break.  This revolt is about to break out.

Newly built ships are transferred to Liberty Echo by a skeleton crew.  The pirates of the sector have learned of this lapse in security and intend to hijack a Conestoga cruiser from under the UA’s nose.

Designation Skyfire Down Correctional Facility, ORDF shipyard
Affiliation UA, Lunnar-Welsun
Classification Terrestrial, terraformed, temperate, rocky chasms and mines
Population 100,000 inmates, 2,000 administration, 8,000 military
Resources Minerals, heavy metals, helium 3, convict labor

Campaign Hooks: The PCs are prisoners, needing to find a way to escape, or someone in Skyfire Down needs breaking out.  Perhaps they are working with the Royal Marines, or trying to stop the break-out? And that unprotected Conestoga … why should pirates get it, when the PCs might get the chance first?

Khadaji – The Wells

The Khadaji system is home to Wells colony.  Established in 2124, the colony exports water found in subterranean reservoirs.  The locals rebelled in 2154 only to be crushed by a UA force, acting on the 3WE’s request.  Having secured the colony the Marines never left, and the 3WE wants it back.

However, the water of Wells is more than it appears.  It carries an alien microbe that excretes a powerful hallucinogen.  Reports have been heard of people going off their axle all across the sector, but they haven’t been linked to the water from Wells colony – yet.  The USCMC commander at Wells, Colonel Maia Winter, is aware of the microbe, but hopes to pin the blame on the 3WE.

Lebanon II is not the only moon of the KJ331 gas giant – Adana has chasms revealing mineral riches, Paphos is an irradiated rock, and Cinder glows with volcanism and indigenous life.  The UPP has quietly colonized all three.  They need more supplies for these dangerous settlements, and space truckers to ship them in – tough jobs, but the UPP pays well.

Campaign Hooks: The PCs witness a hallucinogenic outburst – the microbe’s victim stalking the alleys of a base, murdering innocents – and must find the truth.  Will they blow the scandal wide open or use that information for their own ends? Or are they explorers, sent to scout the other moons of KJ331.

Khadaji: The Wells
Affiliation 3WE (UA occupation), Lasalle Bionational, Weyland-Yutani
Classification Terrestrial, terraformed, temperate, Jovian moon
Population 40,000 civilians, 1,000 UA security forces
Resources Iron, uranium, potable water

GJ229A – Torin Prime

Torin Prime didn’t welcome the imposition of UA authority when it was formed in 2104.  Two years later the so-called J’Har Rebellion blew up.  The rebels were crushed, dissidents left to rot in the notorious GR161 prison camp.  It says something about the J’Har’s resilience that GR161 is as full now as it was 75 years ago.

An independent government in exile, under President Araceli Segarra, makes the J’Har’s case, while another faction, under Para Guarani, turned to piracy.

Torin holds a secret – a vast supply of rhenium, vital for superalloys used in mega construction.  The UA can’t exploit it as the rebels sabotage their operations.  Segarra is dangling the rhenium as a carrot for 3WE and UPP military aid.  Both powers are tempted, but skeptical, and have sent covert missions to Torin Prime to check the J’Har’s claims.

Campaign Hooks: The PCs are rebels, or freelancers trying to make a buck, smuggling the rhenium.  They might work for the UA, tracking down Guarani and Segarra’s agents, or looking to take them out of the equation, or they might be agents for the 3WE or UPP.

GJ229A: Torin Prime
Affiliation UA
Classification Terrestrial, temperate warm, mountainous, forested
Population 700,000 civilians, 50,000 security forces
Resources Rare minerals, heavy metals

NN3325 – Devil’s Peak

NN3325 is littered with barren asteroid fields – the ideal place for Devil’s Peak Station.

The existence of Devil’s Peak is only known within a tight community of morally bankrupt and evil people.  The brainchild of Syran Hosse, CEO of Lunnar-Welsun, Devil’s Peak is an entertainment resort like no other, where the select elite can come and gawp at the XX121 Xenomorph’s brutality.  Buried deep inside an asteroid, Devil’s Peak is a theater of nightmares.

Hosse’s operation needs a steady supply of victims, and he doesn’t much care where he gets them.  Teams of “recruiters” travel the sector, kidnapping those who no one will miss.

Campaign Hooks: One of the PCs’ friends disappears, and they discover Devil’s Peak.  Or they are contracted to deliver a cargo of hypersleeping people to a location in deep space, a strange contract offering a big payday.  Alternatively, they overhear loose talk from a foolish corporate exec, bragging about Devil’s Peak.  What do they do with that information? Can they bargain it for something, and who will come after them if they do? >

NN3325: Devil’s Peak
Affiliation Syran Hosse, Lunnar-Welsun
Classification Giant asteroid
Population 100
Resources XX121 Xenomorphs

Gamma Leporis – Steer City

This trinary system had three colonies, but only Steer City on Gamma Leporis A3 survives.  Colonnade colony orbiting Gamma Leporis B was destroyed by an asteroid, and Seegson’s Wheatfield colony on Homestead, orbiting Gamma Leporis C, was found deserted.  The mystery remains unsolved.  There’s still valuable gear for salvagers and scavengers, and the UPP is planning another colonization attempt.

Steer City thrives in the sweeping fields of Terraform 3, its automated farms producing the food that keeps Tartarus sector fed, making it a tempting target.  The 3WE wants control of the system and is blackmailing the Lasalle chief at Steer City, Pierre Rampier.

The UPP has long had agents in Lasalle’s ranks.  They are ordered to use Lasalle’s own blight virus to devastate Steer City’s agriculture, bringing starvation to the sector.  The blame will be laid squarely at Lasalle Bionational’s door and leave the way open for the UPP to sweep in and save the day.  Who cares about the colonists who will starve as a result?

Campaign Hooks: The PCs are colonists at Steer City and uncover the UPP’s plans, or infiltrators trying to make them happen.  Perhaps they stumble across the conspiracy and must choose what to do.  Wheatfield colony is ripe for exploration and salvage, but what will they find there? And what might be left of Colonnade? Was its destruction an accident, and if not, what secrets might it hide?

Gamma Leporis: Steer City
Affiliation Lasalle Bionational, Seegson, UA security
Classification Terrestrial, terraformed, temperate, plains, hills
Population 9,000 civilians, 250 military
Resources Agriculture

GL408 – Liberty Echo

The UA’s headquarters in Tartarus sector, under the authority of Administrator Prescott Smith, the planet itself is one endless frosty plain.  There is a standing fleet of six Conestoga cruisers, tasked with protecting Tartarus sector and the Far Reach.  It holds a research facility for

Weyland-Yutani’s Weapons Division under Colonel David Fagan, with XX121 specimens on ice, and is also a listening post for Tanburro Station, in the distant 78 Nu Ceti system.

Rumors have hinted at something important going down, so important that the UA has sent four Conestoga cruisers to deal with it.  No one knows where this flotilla is heading, but everyone knows that the UA’s defense fleet in Tartarus now consists of only two cruisers – and their rivals are eager to take advantage of it.

Campaign Hooks: The PCs work for the UA or W-Y or deliver cargo as space truckers.  Perhaps they infiltrate the place, to learn more about the research center or why the UA sent the best part of its fleet away.  Many would pay well for that information.

GL408: Liberty Echo
Affiliation UA, ORDF
Classification Small terrestrial, terraformed, freezing, Jovian moon

GL300 – Linna 349

Settled in 2110 (Harare and Neusheune colonies) Linna is the lynchpin of the 3WE’s ambitions in Tartarus sector.  Linna’s greatest export is timber from the Karyta tree.  However, the wood carries the Yellowbelly beetle, a virulent pest that infests colonies, destroying them from within.   Ten years ago, the local government, under their leader Shane Boulton, declared independence.  Desperate to stop the rebels, the 3WE called upon the UA for help.  In a carbon copy of the Lebanon II crisis, the Colonial Marines took control then refused to step aside.  This outcome was not what either the Boulton rebels or the 3WE wanted.  They have joined forces to drive their common enemy out.  Boulton wants peace and to control his colony’s future.  The 3WE needs to regain control, give the UA a long overdue slap in the face, and bring Boulton to heel.

Campaign Hooks: The PCs are on a ship or base affected by the Yellowbelly beetle, rushing to defeat the infestation, or sent to Linna to acquire some larvae, to be used as a bioweapon.  Or perhaps they are sent by the 3WE to mediate with Boulton, or by the UA to kill him.

GL300: Linna 349
Affiliation 3WE (UA occupation)
Classification Terrestrial, temperate warm, forests, lakes
Population 30,000 civilians, 1,000 UA security

HIP53020 – Pala Station

HIP53020 is home to the archaeological remains of an Engineer settlement and a Juggernaut, as well as dense tropical jungle, and predatory life, in the form of the tiger-like Leon.

Two secret colonies were established – Pala Station to explore the archaeology, and Site Two to examine the remains of the ship, with company ships transporting their finds back to the labs.  But some ships have been lost.  Where are they, and what happened to their cargoes?

Both Lunnar-Welsun and Lasalle Bionational suspect W-Y’s activities on HIP53020.  It’s only a matter of time before their agents uncover something.

W-Y is worried about the 3WE’s new colony on a planet in the same system.  Bethlehem colony, on a world notable only for violent outgassing, is designated as a prospecting mission, but W-Y suspect it’s a surveillance post – something they need to quietly neutralize.

Campaign Hooks: The PCs stumble across one of W-Y’s lost ships, or are contracted as salvagers to find one – what secrets will they discover? Or they work for W-Y on ­LV-895, exploring the ruins or protecting against the Leon.  Alternatively, they may be investigators for Lunnar-Welsun, or scouting the 3WE’s new colony.

HIP53020: Pala Station

HIP51317 – Mendel Station

HIP51317 is only notable as the location of Weyland-Yutani’s Mendel Station, a bioweapons laboratory believed destroyed 45 years ago.  Rumors are circulating that the station survived and is now in the Aventine asteroid field.  W-Y denies the rumors and claims there never was such a facility.

The station rests on the surface of a huge asteroid.  It’s severely damaged but hypersleeping survivors, research and equipment remain intact.  Mendel Station housed XX121 Xenomorphs.  They established a hive, preying on the crew.  Classified reports indicate that the suspected Queen and all her Drones may have died in their decades of abandonment.  Of course, there should still be enough material left to make anyone who finds the site rich.

Weyland-Yutani is putting together a team to get there first.  The 3WE and UPP, and independent salvagers, are doing the same.  It’s a strange race – none admit where they are going – but it’s a race nonetheless, to recover Mendel Station’s secrets.

Campaign Hooks: The PCs are contracted as salvagers or for an exploratory mission, or just see the opportunities for themselves.  Or perhaps someone they know was on the base, and they’d love to learn what happened to them.

HIP51317: Mendel Station
Affiliation Weyland-Yutani
Classification Orbital research station
Population Three (was 350)
Resources Research, equipment, bioweapons, XX121 Xenomorphs

GL257AB – Tartarus

Tartarus colony is a UA mining outfit on a forlorn world of deserts and ravines.  Alongside Seegson and their Working Joe androids, the UA didn’t account for the indigenous life, the Harvesters.  In 2161 a massive herd obliterated the colony.  Having failed to learn from this tragic lesson, the UA tried again ten years later.

This time they were cautious.  However, illegal prospecting outfits sprung up, stripping the planet and leading to the so-called Prospector Wars.  Seeing no other way, the UA accelerated their operations, before the independents picked the planet clean.  Again, the Harvesters reacted aggressively.  Some saw this state of affairs as an opportunity.  Enterprising folk began rounding up the juveniles for sale off-world.  It’s totally illegal, but there’s too much money at stake and no one to stop them.

Campaign Hooks: The PCs want their share of Tartarus’s bounty and go prospecting.  Or they exploit the new Harvester trade and go hunting juveniles.  Alternatively, there are many who’d be willing to pay to see the independent prospectors put out of business.

GJ2034 – Argos

LV-1188 is an icy ball orbiting a red dwarf.  The Independent Core Systems Colonies (ICSC) colonized the planet as neutral ground for all to use without fear or favor.  Under the leadership of colonial supervisor Carol Sherrer, the colony is designed so antagonistic factions can stay apart while Sherrer and her administrators mediate between them.

While Sherrer hasn’t managed to get the UA and 3WE to share the same conference room, Argos colony has been a great success as a hub for trade and transport.  The UA and 3WE maintain a footprint here but challenge the UPP’s unwelcome presence.

Campaign Hooks: The PCs find supplies, repairs, jobs, information, colonial marshals, space truckers, and representatives of all the major corporations here – it’s a melting pot for all who call Tartarus sector home.

Beta Virginis – Rodina

Beta Virginis is illuminated by a large, blue star (Beta Virginis A) and its brown dwarf companion (Beta Virginis B).  Beta Virginis A hosts Rodina, a stunning planet reminiscent of Earth a million years ago.

Two attempts have been made to colonize it, by the 3WE and UA – both failed, the colonists succumbing to Neural Distortion Disorder caused by the host star, and violently harming themselves, or others, or both.  They don’t yet know their colonies have failed.

However, the UPP has established a colony in orbit around Beta Virginis B to study Beta Virginis A.  They intend to settle Rodina for themselves and will colonize as soon as they can mitigate the NDDs.  Cosmos Exploration Corps scout ships patrol the Cusp of Tartarus, to destroy ships heading their way.  Their success has earned this zone of space a new reputation as “the Bermuda Triangle” of Tartarus.

Campaign Hooks: The PCs work for the UPP and are investigating Rodina.  Or they are part of a rescue crew for the silent 3WE and UA colonies or searching for the ships that have gone missing.  Alternatively, they are part of a new colonization attempt and must face the NDDs themselves.
