11-12.description: Industrial gases Propylene, acetylene, propane, ethylformate, chlorofluorocarbon, ammonia, carbon monoxide, ethylene oxide, hydrogen chloride, sulfur dioxide, sulfur hexafluoride.

13-14.name: CARGO
13-14.description: Metal ingots or pellets Gold, platinum, palladium, silver, tungsten, copper, iron, etc.

15-16.name: CARGO
15-16.description: Colonists Humans in stasis, ready to begin a colonization project

21-21.name: CARGO
21-21.description: Timber Exotic alien tree products destined for Earth

22-22.name: CARGO
22-22.description: Ice/Water Water, water ice or some other rare frozen solution

23-23.name: CARGO
23-23.description: Industrial chemicalsAluminium Chloride, Aluminium Sulfate, Calcium Acetate, Monosodium Phosphate, Ferric Sulphate, Sodium Hydroxide, Hydrochloric Acid, Sodium Aluminate, Polyaluminium Chloride, Ferrous Chloride, Borate, Potassium Acetate etc.

24-24.name: CARGO
24-24.description: Fertilizer Multi-nutrient fertilizer compounds made up of nitrogen, potassium and/or phosphate

25-26.name: CARGO
25-26.description: Oil Crude oil, or liquid petroleum by-products

31-32.name: CARGO
31-32.description: Foodstuff Bulk foods such as chickpeas, soybeans and other legumes, grains (corn, barley, rice, wheat) or refined versions thereof

33-36.name: CARGO
33-36.description: Ore. Bauxite (aluminum), galena (lead), pentlandite (nickel), gold-quartz, cassiterite (tin), malachite (copper), magnetite (iron), platinum-bearing sand, trimonite (tungsten)

41-41.name: CARGO
41-41.description: Medicinal goods Vaccines, medicines, disinfectants, surgical gear, scanning machines, hospital beds

42-43.name: CARGO
42-43.description: Technical parts Different makes and types, for suits, refineries, vehicles, power stations, hospitals, prospecting gear, factories, atmospheric processors, weaponry or life support systems

44-45.name: CARGO
44-45.description: Starship technical parts Modules, features, parts for/from dismantled ships

46-46.name: CARGO
46-46.description: Pressure suits Space suits for delivery to the colonies

51-51.name: CARGO
51-51.description: Single oversized item Wind turbines, power station generator, space station hull frame, solar panel assembly, drilling machinery, ore processing mill or furnace

52-52.name: CARGO
52-52.description: Vehicles Diggers, tractors, quad-tracks, all-terrain vehicles, power loaders

53-54.name: CARGO
53-54.description: Weapons & Armor Firearms, ammunition and armor for the colonies or remote stations

55-56.name: CARGO
55-56.description: Radioactives Processed uranium cakes or uranium dioxide powder, or fusion plant fuel pellets such as deuterium, tritium, protium or helium-3

61-62.name: CARGO
61-62.description: Colony Construction Beams, modules, airlocks, outer shells, roofing material, etc.

63-63.name: CARGO
63-63.description: Animal Feed Feed concentrates containing grains, high-protein oil meals and byproducts of sugar beet and sugarcane processing

64-65.name: CARGO
64-65.description: Livestock/Animals Cattle in stasis, ready for rearing on an off-world colony

66-66.name: CARGO
66-66.description: Wreckage/Salvage Shuttle, or escape/cargo pod requiring investigation and study

11-13.name: COMPLICATION
11-13.description: Embargo/Quarantine The destination is placed under quarantine or an embargo.

14-16.name: COMPLICATION
14-16.description: Intermission The ship’s computer brings the ship out of hyperspace early, and then wakes the crew. What’s the story?

21-26.name: COMPLICATION
21-26.description: Military A military starship sends over a small search party for a “routine” ICC and customs check. Should the PCs be worried?

31-43.name: COMPLICATION
31-43.description: Maintenance A critical part (drive pump, plasma coil, coolant pump, water recycler, gravity compensator control unit, sensor gimbal motor, etc.) requires replacement before it fails, requiring most of the crew’s participation.

44-53.name: COMPLICATION
44-53.description: Waiting Game Problems at the destination mean they aren’t ready to accept the cargo. Can the crew help speed things along?

54-56.name: COMPLICATION
54-56.description: Cargo Mishap There is a serious problem with the cargo, either moving, leaking, over-heating or catching fire.

61-66.name: COMPLICATION
61-66.description: Wreckage A small piece of wreckage is spotted on the sensor scope; a cargo container, escape pod, frozen corpse, part of a starship—smashed or blown off, etc.

11-13.name: DESTINATION
11-13.description: Only Coordinates. Coordinates for an area in deep space.

14-16.name: DESTINATION
14-16.description: Hostile Forest/Jungle/Desert Landing site is planet-side wilderness, far from human habitation, or on an uninhabited world.

21-26.name: DESTINATION
21-26.description: Mine A mining facility, far from a colony or starport.

31-33.name: DESTINATION
31-33.description: Spaceport Spaceport on an asteroid or moon, or a landing field near a larger settlement.

34-36.name: DESTINATION
34-36.description: Asteroid/Moon The surface of an asteroid or a small moon. Vacuum or dangerous atmosphere.

44-46.name: DESTINATION
44-46.description: Earth, Gateway Station. The busy hub of interstellar traffic and commerce.

51-53.name: DESTINATION
51-53.description: Young Colony A small colony with only a few hundred inhabitants.

54-56.name: DESTINATION
54-56.description: Established Colony A busy colony with several thousand people and a thriving, local industry.

64-66.name: DESTINATION
64-66.description: Outpost A small outpost, usually planetside. An outpost is commonly just a single complex with a specific function; corporate, military or scientific.

61-63.name: DESTINATION
61-63.description: Starship. A starship in orbit, awaiting your arrival

3-3.description: Weyland-Yutani

4-4.description: Gorham

5-6.description: They stole it from one of the other companies, and they know.

11-21.name: COMPLICATION
11-21.description: Natural Phenomenon Some severe natural event occurs during the mission: a rapid temperature change, forest fire, hurricane, tsunami, earthquake, mudslide, etc.

22-32.name: COMPLICATION
22-32.description: Survey Blues The target area is either difficult to locate, or difficult to survey safely or scol3iciently.

33-35.name: COMPLICATION
33-35.description: Presumed Missing If the PCs gained a permit to survey their target area, they may or may not realize it is inherited from a previous expedition that vanished without a trace.

36-44.name: COMPLICATION
36-44.description: Rival Expedition A competing party has the same goal as the expedition and tries to get there first or stop the PCs. They have roughly the same gear as the PCs.

45-52.name: COMPLICATION
45-52.description: Quarantine The target area is under quarantine or off-limits, possibly for reasons unknown. The expedition has no permit and will be breaking the law if they choose to proceed.

53-62.name: COMPLICATION
53-62.description: Deadly Treasure Some terrible object(s) exist in the target area, unbeknownst to the PCs. This deadly find may be nuclear waste, a dump of biological weapons, a nest of Xenomorph eggs or something equally horrific and life-threatening!

63-66.name: COMPLICATION
63-66.description: Surveillance The expedition is under surveillance by the military, government or some other party. They will not intervene, although they may communicate their presence to the team. Why are they watching? What do they really want?

11-14.name: DESTINATION
11-14.description: Abandoned Orbital Station Forgotten, abandoned, barely operational.

15-21.name: DESTINATION
15-21.description: Rogue Asteroid A fast-moving interstellar asteroid or planet passing through a star system.

22-24.name: DESTINATION
22-24.description: Abandoned Mine A failed mining project with tunnels and buildings, now abandoned and decaying.

25-31.name: DESTINATION
25-31.description:
DESCRIPTION:
Moon The rocky moon of a gas giant or planet.

32-35.name: DESTINATION
32-35.description: Asteroid Belt An asteroid that sits deep within a dense asteroid belt.

36-36.name: DESTINATION
36-36.description: Colonized World The target area sits in wilderness on a world that already contains colonists.

41-43.name: DESTINATION
41-43.description: Terrestrial Planet The target area sits on an uninhabited terrestrial planet.

44-44.name: DESTINATION
44-44.description: Abandoned Colony A failed colony with buildings and structures abandoned and decaying.

45-51.name: DESTINATION
45-51.description: Ice Planet The target area sits on an uninhabited ice planet.

52-63.description: Wreckage The smashed wreckage of a spacecraft. Roll D6 for type and roll on the destination table again for its current location.
52-63.name: EV - CR STARSHIP

64-66.description: Outpost. A small outpost, usually planet side. An outpost is commonly just a single complex with a specific function; corporate, military or scientific.

6-6.description: Independent Core Systems Colonies (ICSC)

11-16.name: MISSION
11-16.description: Salvage Locate an abandoned or destroyed ship, station or planetary facility. Recover items of value and avoid the wreck’s fate…

21-24.name: MISSION
21-24.description: Survey Map a location or an area for the employer. Report back with sensor maps and other collected data.

25-32.name: MISSION
25-32.description: Mining Begin test-mining to determine the viability for later investors. The substance being recovered may be cobalt, gold, tungsten, oil, natural gas, lead or something else.

33-36.name: MISSION
33-36.description: Colony Assistance Assist a start-up colony with gear, information or expert knowledge about surface exploration, medicine, prospecting, construction or something else.

41-45.name: MISSION
41-45.description: Prospecting Command a prospecting expedition or secure a claim somewhere. It could be mining, asteroid harvesting, logging or gas trawling.

46-52.name: MISSION
46-52.description: Data Collection Find a specific piece of information for the employer. Sometimes, the group does not know the intended use of the information.

53-55.name: MISSION
53-55.description: Courier Make sure sensitive information, resources or goods are delivered safely from the employer to the receiver—without delay.

56-62.name: MISSION
56-62.description: Anomaly Exploration A unique phenomenon requires speedy investigation—is it a threat, or something that can be exploited for profit? It may be a wormhole, gravity lens, powerful radiation emission or other anomaly.

63-66.name: MISSION
63-66.description: Rescue Expedition Rescue a group, colony, survey expedition or correspondents from an attack or some other peril. Often, the PCs will be unaware of the fate of the missing victims.

3-4.description: They are in big trouble (not their fault).

5-6.description: They’re in big trouble (and it’s definitely their own fault). What did they do?

1-1.name: BONUS REWARD - Used for mercenary outfits, not employed USCMC personnel
1-1.description: Faction contact

2-2.name: BONUS REWARD - Used for mercenary outfits, not employed USCMC personnel
2-2.description: Ship module

3-4.name: BONUS REWARD - Used for mercenary outfits, not employed USCMC personnel

5-6.name: BONUS REWARD - Used for mercenary outfits, not employed USCMC personnel

11-12.name: COMPLICATION
11-12.description: Role Reversal The marines find out that the bad guys are actually good guys.

13-15.name: COMPLICATION
13-15.description: Intermission The ship’s computer brings the ship out of hyperspace early, and then wakes the crew. What’s the story?

16-16.name: COMPLICATION
16-16.description: Observer The team is saddled with a reporter/cameraman or a senior officer who gets in the way and asks stupid questions.

21-23.name: COMPLICATION
21-23.description: Company Meddling A corporate representative joins the team and is there to ensure the company’s assets and interests are protected.

24-25.name: COMPLICATION
24-25.description: Civilian Advisor Technical knowledge or on-site advice is provided by a civilian advisor who has little knowledge of military operations. They may get scared or panic easily.

26-32.name: COMPLICATION
26-32.description: Captured An NPC or even a PC is captured by hostile forces.

33-36.name: COMPLICATION
33-36.description: Gear Problems The team has faulty gear. It could be anything from ammo or weapons to sensors or vehicles.

41-44.name: COMPLICATION
41-44.description: Tough Resistance The opponents are far tougher and more ruthless than expected.

45-46.name: COMPLICATION
45-46.description: Trapped During the mission, the team discovers that it is completely trapped, either physically, or tactically.

51-53.name: COMPLICATION
51-53.description: Under Fire! The mission location is hit by an air-strike, mines, or heavy weapons, possibly the result of a mishap by their own forces!

54-55.name: COMPLICATION
54-55.description: Glory Hound A new commanding office, a lieutenant, is keen to get himself a medal or commendation, and pushes the marine squad into perilous situations. Someone is going to get killed!

56-62.name: COMPLICATION
56-62.description: Traps There are hidden dangers across the mission site, varying with the nature of the location. They may be mines, IEDs, predatory carnivorous plants or improvised booby traps.

63-64.name: COMPLICATION
63-64.description: Restrictions There are tactical restrictions placed on the mission—how the squad acts, where it can go, what weapons it can use, etc.

65-66.name: COMPLICATION
65-66.description: Green Commander A new platoon commander is a green, untested and untried lieutenant. He’s read the books, survived the training and ran the simulations—but he’ll go to pieces once the bullets start flying.

11-23.name: DESTINATION
11-23.description: Colony Either an established or young colony.

24-26.name: DESTINATION
24-26.description: Isolated Outpost A research station or remote military outpost.

31-32.name: DESTINATION
31-32.description: Starship in Orbit An enemy ship, or perhaps an abandoned ship.

33-34.name: DESTINATION
33-34.description: Orbital Space Station A transfer station, space colony or orbital survey platform.

35-36.name: DESTINATION
35-36.description: Wilderness Location Far from civilization, a remote spot on a planetary surface.

41-43.name: DESTINATION
41-43.description: Planetary Warzone An active war zone, fought between colonies, corporations or nation states, with ruined buildings, wrecked vehicles and fortifications.

44-46.name: DESTINATION
44-46.description: Isolated Spaceport A landing field far from any colony, owned by a corporation, individual or military.

51-52.name: DESTINATION
51-52.description: Scattered Homesteads Colonial farmsteads, far from civilization and scattered across the planetary surface.

56-61.name: DESTINATION
56-61.description: Prison Complex Remote penal colony, housing hardened and violent inmates.

53-55.name: DESTINATION
53-55.description: Mine and Refinery A huge mining and refining complex, with hundreds of workers and executives.

62-63.name: DESTINATION
62-63.description: Radar/Sensor Site An automated sensor site, perhaps with its own defenses.

64-66.name: DESTINATION
64-66.description: Impenetrable Area Harsh, inhospitable wilderness such as thick jungle, deep caverns or volcanic lava fields.

11-13.name: MISSION
11-13.description: Recon Scout a location, gather intelligence and then report back.

14-15.name: MISSION
14-15.description: Assault Attack and hold an objective by force.

16-21.name: MISSION
16-21.description: Defense Defend a location/person/group and repel any attack until relieved or until a set time.

22-23.name: MISSION
22-23.description: Combat Patrol Patrol an area, looking for signs of the enemy.

24-26.name: MISSION
24-26.description: Sabotage Infiltrate an enemy location and destroy a key asset (bridge, uplink tower, radar dish, etc.)

31-32.name: MISSION
31-32.description: Raid Create chaos and destruction by attacking targets of opportunity behind enemy lines.

33-35.name: MISSION
33-35.description: Search and Rescue Search for a downed pilot, lost colonists, etc.

36-42.name: MISSION
36-42.description: Peace-Keeping Quell a riot and re-establishing order, or protect lines of communication and essential services until authority can be restored.

43-46.name: MISSION
43-46.description: Bug Hunt Exterminate local alien life that is threatening colonists on an off-world planet.

51-52.name: MISSION
51-52.description: Civil Evacuation A colonial or space station population needs immediate rescue from a crisis or natural catastrophe.

53-54.name: MISSION
53-54.description: Space Assault A space station, orbital platform or starship must be captured (or recaptured) by boarding it and seizing control.

55-55.name: MISSION
55-55.description: Space Traffic Security The marines are aboard a military vessel that makes customs and security checks on civilian ships in the area, looking for illegal drugs or other goods, arms, workers being trafficked etc.

56-62.name: MISSION
56-62.description: Snatch and Grab Locate and seize an item, person or group from behind enemy lines. It may be hostages, POWs, an enemy commander or a piece of high technology.

63-66.name: MISSION
63-66.description: Investigation A station, colony or installation is not responding to Network communications. Investigate.

5-6.description: They offer the PCs a way to make some money.

11-13.name: AND EXPERIENCED
11-13.description:
A stroke of luck that made your life easy or boosted your prospects.

  • +1 HEAVY MACHINERY, +1 MOBILITY,
  • +2 to your psych evaluation roll

14-16.name: AND EXPERIENCED
14-16.description:
Life as the plaything of a rich dignitary or organization executive.

  • +1 MANIPULATION, +1 PILOTING,
  • +1 to your psych evaluation roll

21-23.name: AND EXPERIENCED
21-23.description:
A job that you didn’t hate, that had hopes of advancement and the chance to better your lifestyle.

  • +1 STAMINA, +1 SURVIVAL,
  • +1 to your psych evaluation roll

24-26.name: AND EXPERIENCED
24-26.description:
The opportunity to make someone else’s life better, but at a significant personal cost.

  • +1 MEDICAL AID, +1 COMMAND

31-33.name: AND EXPERIENCED
31-33.description:
Time in prison for a crime you may (or may not) have committed, or locked away in a warehouse with other unwanted androids.

  • +1 CLOSE COMBAT, +1 SURVIVAL

34-36.name: AND EXPERIENCED
34-36.description:
A period of slave labor, under the lash of a brutal chain gang boss.

  • +1 STAMINA, +1 OBSERVATION

41-43.name: AND EXPERIENCED
41-43.description:
Tedious years in space, working for peanuts and forever suffering hypersleep sickness or soul-sucking loneliness.

  • +1 PILOTING, +1 HEAVY MACHINERY

44-46.name: AND EXPERIENCED
44-46.description:
Isolation on an abandoned colony, having to do unspeakable things just to survive.

  • +1 CLOSE COMBAT, +1 COMTECH

51-53.name: AND EXPERIENCED
51-53.description:
Years as a low-level stooge, watching the workers die as you made them do the deadly jobs.

  • +1 COMMAND, +1 RANGED COMBAT

54-56.name: AND EXPERIENCED
54-56.description:
A science facility where you were a test subject, suffering painful and dangerous procedures.

  • +1 MOBILITY, +1 COMTECH, –1 to your psych evaluation roll

61-63.name: AND EXPERIENCED
61-63.description:
A no-win situation where you killed someone or through inaction let them die.

  • +1 RANGED COMBAT, +1 MANIPULATION,
  • –1 to your psych evaluation roll

64-66.name: AND EXPERIENCED
64-66.description:
Time on an isolated research station that malfunctioned, releasing test subjects that wreaked havoc.

  • +1 OBSERVATION, +1 MEDICAL AID,
  • –2 to your psych evaluation roll

11-12.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
11-12.description:
You live a charmed life – long may this continue! Gain [[2d6*50}} W-Y dollars, a bonus roll on the Career Gear column of your choice,
+2 to psych evaluation roll.


+1 Strength,
+1 Empathy

13-14.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
13-14.description:
You commit a crime and think you’ve got away with it.
+1 to psych evaluation roll.

+1 Strength,
+1 Wits

15-16.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
15-16.description:
Someone pulls some strings, and you get a place in a specialist school or company college. You gain 1 point in a random general skill.

+1 to psych evaluation roll.

+1 Strength,
+1 Agility

21-22.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
21-22.description:
You commit a crime and get caught. You cut a deal and get released, but now you’re in debt to someone.

+1 Agility,
+1 Wits

23-24.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
23-24.description:
You read Space Beast and draw the attention of a Weyland-Yutani exec, who tells you to keep your mouth shut – unless you want to join the team. He leaves you his card, just in case.

+1 Wits,
+1 Empathy

25-26.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
25-26.description:
You survive a serious illness but now cannot abide dirt and grime – they harbor deadly bugs.

+1 Agility,
+1 Empathy

31-32.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
31-32.description:
You survive a terrible crash. Now you always demand to be the driver or pilot.

+1 Strength,
+1 Agility

33-34.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
33-34.description:
You wake from hypersleep to find your crew has died. It was nothing to do with you, but no one believes it.

+1 Strength,
+1 Wits>

35-36.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
35-36.description:
You find an official secret. Do you keep it, sell it on the black market, or trade it in for favors?

+1 Strength,
+1 Empathy

41-42.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
41-42.description:
You scam someone of something valuable, and as far as the law is concerned have done nothing wrong. But they want it back.

+1 Wits,
+1 Empathy

43-44.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
43-44.description:
A seismic event destroys your home. Was this a bad thing, destroying your one place of comfort, or did it help you escape the slums?

+1 Agility,
+1 Empathy

45-46.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
45-46.description:
An industrial accident leaves you trapped. Now you suffer mild claustrophobia.

+1 Agility,
+1 Wits

51-52.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
51-52.description:
You earned enough credits to escape the colony where you work, until they doubled the quota. Your hatred for your oppressors burns fiercely.

+1 Strength,
+1 Agility

53-54.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
53-54.description:
You kill someone, or through inaction let them die, and it lies heavy on your conscience.
–1 to your psych evaluation roll.

+1 Wits,
+1 Empathy

55-56.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
55-56.description:
You survive a fire with horrible burns. Do you fear fire? Or do you love watching it burn?
–1 to your psych evaluation roll.

+1 Strength,
+1 Wits

61-62.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
61-62.description:
Involved in an industrial accident, someone saves you but pays with their life. You witness their death. Since then, you have told yourself you couldn’t save them, but did you really try?

–1 to your psych evaluation roll.

+1 Agility,
+1 Wits

63-64.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
63-64.description:
You’re abandoned and left to die. This betrayal has wounded you so deeply that now you trust no one. Perhaps you want revenge on those who betrayed you.
–2 to your psych evaluation roll.

+1 Strength,
+1 Empathy

65-66.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
65-66.description:
You come face to face with beastly monsters, but escape. The creatures haunt your dreams. No one believes a word of it, that is, if you even chose to tell anyone.
–2 to your psych evaluation roll.

+1 Agility,
+1 Empathy

EV - 34. LIFE PATH - RANDOM GENERAL SKIL.name: EV - 34. LIFE PATH - RANDOM GENERAL SKILLS

55-56.name: EVENT/ATTRIBUTES
55-56.description:
You survive a fire with horrible burns. Do you fear fire? Or do you love watching it burn?
–1 to your psych evaluation roll.

+1 Strength,
+1 Wits

Oy2TmQooCu5zltgb.name: EV - LP IN THE COMPANY OF

1-1.name: FAVOR
1-1.description: Popular. Gain +1 bonus to MANIPULATION when dealing with your organization.

2-2.name: FAVOR
2-2.description: Free Rein In The Company Warehouse. Make an additional gear roll for your career.

3-3.name: FAVOR
3-3.description: Generalist Training Program. You gain 1 point in a random general skill, but owe someone a favor for getting you in.

4-4.name: FAVOR
4-4.description: Specialist Training Program. You gain 1 point in a random career skill, but owe someone a favor for getting you in.

5-5.name: FAVOR
5-5.description: Bonus. Make an additional paycheck roll. But don’t let this success go to your head, as others envy you.

6-6.name: FAVOR
6-6.description: New Friend. Someone owes you a favor. But are they really your pal? Can you trust them?

1-1.name: DISASTERS
1-1.description: Injured. By accident or someone’s design you are severely hurt. Lose 1 attribute point from either Strength or Agility.

2-2.name: DISASTERS
2-2.description: Trauma. You can’t forget a terrifying incident. Lose 1 attribute point from either Wits or Empathy.

3-3.name: DISASTERS
3-3.description: Lost Something. Lose a random item of equipment.

4-4.name: DISASTERS
4-4.description: Misfortune. Someone dies, and you are blamed. Branded a Jonah, no one will work with someone cursed with ill-fortune.

5-5.name: DISASTERS
5-5.description: Nemesis. A rival stitches you up, and you are sacked. Time to join the big bad world.

6-6.name: DISASTERS
6-6.description: Sacked. Either through negligence or incompetence your contract is canceled. Time to join the big bad world.

EV - 37. LIFE PATH - POSTINGS COLONIAL M.name: EV - 37. LIFE PATH - POSTINGS COLONIAL MARINE

1-1.name: CAREER POSTINGS
1-1.description: Garrison Duty. Tedious but safe.

2-2.name: CAREER POSTINGS
2-2.description: Colonial Defense. Just another bug hunt, dangerous and no one wants to do it.

3-3.name: CAREER POSTINGS
3-3.description: Peacekeeping. Winning hearts and minds.

4-4.name: CAREER POSTINGS
4-4.description: Population Control. Full scale riot suppression, bashing the strikers.

5-5.name: CAREER POSTINGS
5-5.description: Assault Operations. Lightning raids and nuking from orbit. Make a bonus career gear roll.

6-6.name: CAREER POSTINGS
6-6.description: Combat Operations. On the frontline, nose to nose with your enemies. Make a bonus career gear roll.

EV - 38. LIFE PATH - POSTINGS COLONIAL M.name: EV - 38. LIFE PATH - POSTINGS COLONIAL MARSHAL

1-1.name: CAREER POSTINGS
1-1.description: Backwater Posting. There’s nothing to investigate here, waste of time.

2-2.name: CAREER POSTINGS
2-2.description: Frontier Policing. Nothing but drunks and bar brawls.

3-3.name: CAREER POSTINGS
3-3.description: Authority’s Stooge. You’re not fighting crime, you’re doing the company’s dirty work.

4-4.name: CAREER POSTINGS
4-4.description: Lawless Frontier. It’s you against the gangs, ­corporations, and racketeers.

5-5.name: CAREER POSTINGS
5-5.description: Big Colony Beat. Urban policing, thankless and dangerous. Make a bonus career gear roll.

6-6.name: CAREER POSTINGS
6-6.description: Roving Marshal. You go where the big crimes are. Make a bonus career gear roll.

EV - 39. LIFE PATH - POSTINGS COMPANY AG.name: EV - 39. LIFE PATH - POSTINGS COMPANY AGENT

1-1.name: CAREER POSTINGS
1-1.description: Filing. The worst job, but who knows what you might find in the files.

2-2.name: CAREER POSTINGS
2-2.description: Seconded. A flunkey’s job and you’re going nowhere, unless you can learn something interesting.

3-3.name: CAREER POSTINGS
3-3.description: Recruitment. A shit job, but you know everyone.

4-4.name: CAREER POSTINGS
4-4.description: Exec Without Portfolio. You go where you want, chasing the next big thing.

5-5.name: CAREER POSTINGS
5-5.description: Special Ops. Working for top secret facilities and the weapons division. Make a bonus career gear roll.

6-6.name: CAREER POSTINGS
6-6.description: Troubleshooter. Making surprise visits to corporate outfits, and enjoying the power. Make a bonus career gear roll.

1-1.name: CAREER POSTINGS
1-1.description: Bad Kid. You spend time in juvenile detention.

2-2.name: CAREER POSTINGS
2-2.description: Troubled Kid. Making trouble to hold off the boredom, you’re not popular.

3-3.name: CAREER POSTINGS
3-3.description: Put To Work. Thrown into a shit job to keep you out of mischief, it’s no fun.

4-4.name: CAREER POSTINGS
4-4.description: School’s Out. You do your classes but play hard too. There’s no stopping you once school’s out.

5-5.name: CAREER POSTINGS
5-5.description: Permanent ­Vacation. Free to do what you want, it’s a great way to live. Make a bonus career gear roll.

6-6.name: CAREER POSTINGS
6-6.description: On Your Own. No one cares what you do, as long as you’re out of sight. It’s fun and you find all sorts of things. Make a bonus career gear roll.

1-1.name: CAREER POSTINGS
1-1.description: Disaster Relief. You wait for ages, then are too late to help anybody. Soul destroying job.

2-2.name: CAREER POSTINGS
2-2.description: Bad Side Of Town. It’s rough and no one wants your help, you have to watch your back.

3-3.name: CAREER POSTINGS
3-3.description: Lawless Frontier. Gunshot and stab wounds are your stock in trade.

4-4.name: CAREER POSTINGS
4-4.description: Training School. You’re an instructor but your students don’t care.

5-5.name: CAREER POSTINGS
5-5.description: Military. You run with the grunts, keeping them and yourself alive. Make a bonus career gear roll.

6-6.name: CAREER POSTINGS
6-6.description: Industrial Paramedic. Keeping the workers alive and productive. Make a bonus career gear roll.

1-1.name: CAREER POSTINGS
1-1.description: Security Detail. A dead-end job, a punishment posting.

2-2.name: CAREER POSTINGS
2-2.description: Prison Detail. Putting the convicts to productive work is a challenge when you can only kill a few of them.

3-3.name: CAREER POSTINGS
3-3.description: Colony Teams. Getting things done on the frontier doesn’t make you popular.

4-4.name: CAREER POSTINGS
4-4.description: Tough Decisions. You make the big decisions and get the job done, even if some of your team don’t make it.

5-5.name: CAREER POSTINGS
5-5.description: Cool Head. Disaster strikes, you lead those involved until rescue arrives. Make a bonus career gear roll.

6-6.name: CAREER POSTINGS
6-6.description: Big Boss. You lead a large team doing a dangerous job on the Frontier. Make a bonus career gear roll.

1-1.name: CAREER POSTINGS
1-1.description: Dusting Crops. Shit work in a shit place, and no prospects.

2-2.name: CAREER POSTINGS
2-2.description: Cargo Hauling. Short haul drops of toilet paper and ­toothpaste won’t make your career.

3-3.name: CAREER POSTINGS
3-3.description: Smuggler. It pays the bills if you don’t get caught.

4-4.name: CAREER POSTINGS
4-4.description: Space Truckers. Piloting the interstellar haulers is a tough and respected job, but the pay is shit.

5-5.name: CAREER POSTINGS
5-5.description: Military. Flying dropships and ­dropping nukes keeps you on your toes. Make a bonus career gear roll.

6-6.name: CAREER POSTINGS
6-6.description: Chauffeur. Pilot to the rich and important, you take your boss wherever they want to go. Make a bonus career gear roll.

1-1.name: CAREER POSTINGS
1-1.description: Colony Miner. Working in the dark and in the toxic fumes is a job, at least.

2-2.name: CAREER POSTINGS
2-2.description: Lawless Colony. Nothing works, you can never fix it all, and everyone blames you.

3-3.name: CAREER POSTINGS
3-3.description: Stevedore. Cargo gets nowhere without you. Some gets lost, and you get blamed.

4-4.name: CAREER POSTINGS
4-4.description: Wrecking Crew. Salvaging earns you more than the company dime.

5-5.name: CAREER POSTINGS
5-5.description: Hauler Engineer. Space trucking is a good job, pays okay, and you sleep most of the time. Make a bonus career gear roll.

6-6.name: CAREER POSTINGS
6-6.description: Big Colony Maintenance. You keep the lights on, the air breathable, and folks are glad for it. Make a bonus career gear roll.

1-1.name: CAREER POSTINGS
1-1.description: Backwater Lab. The lowest lab tech, you do the cleaning.

2-2.name: CAREER POSTINGS
2-2.description: Lawless Colony. Science officer is a good job, but not in a shithole colony.

3-3.name: CAREER POSTINGS
3-3.description: Headhunted. You’re hired for a secret project that goes well, until you’re fired.

4-4.name: CAREER POSTINGS
4-4.description: Science Officer. Space haulers need you, and the pay is decent for sleeping for a living.

5-5.name: CAREER POSTINGS
5-5.description: Pristine Lab. Assigned to the best facilities, your research goes far. Make a bonus career gear roll.

6-6.name: CAREER POSTINGS
6-6.description: Field Research. Part of a well-funded team out in the field. Make a bonus career gear roll.

0-0.name: PSYCH EVALUATION
0-0.description: Dangerous, unstable, volatile, prone to psychotic outbursts.

1-1.name: PSYCH EVALUATION
1-1.description: Flashbacks and hallucinations, unhinged and unpredictable.

2-2.name: PSYCH EVALUATION
2-2.description: Defensive, reactive to minor slights, prone to angry outbursts. An untrustworthy worker.

3-4.name: PSYCH EVALUATION
3-4.description: Night sweats, nightmares, distressing outbursts. Temperamental and self-pitying.

5-6.name: PSYCH EVALUATION
5-6.description: Mild trauma, nightmares, nervous episodes. Disruptive, likely to bellyache and bitch.

9-10.name: PSYCH EVALUATION
9-10.description: Positive and compliant. Follows orders for an easy life.

11-12.name: PSYCH EVALUATION
11-12.description: Invested in their work. Keen, ambitious, worthy of promotion.

13-13.name: PSYCH EVALUATION
13-13.description: Zealously enthusiastic, confident bordering on arrogance. Too keen to please – what are they hiding?

14-20.name: PSYCH EVALUATION
14-20.description: Supportive of officialdom to the point of fanaticism. Suspect use of illegal mood enhancers. Warrants close monitoring.

1-6.description: KEEPING IT TOGETHER: You manage to keep your nerves in check. Barely.

7-7.description: NERVOUS TWITCH: Your STRESS LEVEL, and the STRESS LEVEL of all friendly PCs in SHORT range of you, increases by one.'

8-8.description: TREMBLE: You start to tremble uncontrollably. All skill rolls using AGILITY suffer a –2 modification until your panic stops.

9-9.description: DROP ITEM: Whether by stress, confusion or the realization that you’re all going to die anyway, you drop a weapon or other important item—the GM decides which one. Your STRESS LEVEL increases by one.

10-10.description: FREEZE: You’re frozen by fear or stress for one Round, losing your next slow action. Your STRESS LEVEL, and the STRESS LEVEL of all friendly PCs in SHORT range of you, increases by one

11-11.description: SEEK COVER: You must use your next action to move away from danger and find a safe spot if possible. You are allowed to make a retreat roll (see page 93) if you have an enemy at ENGAGED range. Your STRESS LEVEL is decreased by one, but the STRESS LEVEL of all friendly PCs in SHORT range increases by one. After one Round, you can act normally.

12-12.description: SCREAM: You scream your lungs out for one Round, losing your next slow action. Your STRESS LEVEL is decreased by one, but every friendly character who hears your scream must make an immediate Panic Roll.

13-13.description: FLEE: You just can’t take it anymore. You must flee to a safe place and refuse to leave it. You won’t attack anyone and won’t attempt anything dangerous. You are not allowed to make a retreat roll (see page 93) if you have an enemy at ENGAGED range when you flee. Your STRESS LEVEL is decreased by one, but every friendly character who sees you run must make an immediate Panic Roll.

14-14.description: BERSERK: You must immediately attack the nearest person or creature, friendly or not. You won’t stop until you or the target is Broken. Every friendly character who witnesses your rampage must make an immediate Panic Roll

15-20.description: CATATONIC: You collapse to the floor and can’t talk or move, staring blankly into oblivion.

11-13.description:
Confused.

–1 die on all skill rolls based on Wits.

21-23.description:
Reclusive.

You cannot relieve stress in the presence of others.

24-26.description:
Obsessive.

You must push every skill roll – even if it was successful.

33-34.description:
Alcoholic.

You can only relieve stress by drinking alcohol.

41-43.description:
Worrisome.

Even minor concerns (GM’s choice) count as traumatic events for you, giving you +1 stress level.

44-44.description:
Changed Personality.

You get a new personal agenda ), determined by the GM or randomly generated.

45-46.description:
Phobic.

You become phobic of something connected to your trauma (GM’s choice). Every contact with your phobia counts as a traumatic event for you, triggering a panic roll.

51-52.description:
Speech Loss.

You cannot speak and need to communicate using written notes or hand signs.

53-54.description:
Nightmares.

Every shift you sleep, you gain +1 stress level.

55-56.description:
Flashbacks.

Each time you gain stress, you increase the amount by +1.

61-62.description:
Panic Attacks.

If you have rolled a result of 1 or higher (instead of 9 or higher) on a panic roll during a game session, you must make an Empathy roll after the session to avoid mental trauma.

63-63.description:
Violent.

All rolls of 8 or higher on the panic table will trigger the Frenzy response (#14).

64-64.description:
Psychotic.

At some point every Shift (GM’s choice), you experience hallucinations that give you +1 stress level.

65-65.description:
Amnesiac.

You cannot remember who you or the other player characters are. The effect must be roleplayed.

66-66.description:
Personality Split.

Create a new character with a different name, Wits and Empathy scores, a personal agenda, and a random talent. You switch personality every time you gain stress.

2-2.description: Roll for two danger events and danger level +2

3-4.description: Roll for one danger event and danger level +1

EV - 57. LS - SOLO STRESS RESPONSE TABLE.name: EV - 57. LS - SOLO STRESS RESPONSE TABLE

1-1.description:
Jumpy.

When you push a skill roll, you gain +2 stress level instead of +1.

2-2.description:
Tunnel Vision.

All skill rolls based on Wits get –2 dice.

3-3.description:
Aggravated.

All skill rolls based on Empathy get –2 dice.

4-4.description:
Shakes.

All skill rolls based on Agility get –2 dice.

5-5.description:
Frantic.

All skill rolls based on Strength get –2 dice.

6-6.description:
Deflated.

You cannot push any skill rolls. If you are Jumpy (#1 above), remove that response, and ignore any further Jumpy results while Deflated.

7-20.description:
Mess Up.

Your action fails regardless of rolled and you gain +1 stress level.

EV - 58. LS - SOLO PANIC RESPONSE TABLE.name: EV - 58. LS - SOLO PANIC RESPONSE TABLE

1-1.name: Spooked.
1-1.description: Stress level +1 for you.

2-2.name: Noisy.
2-2.description: If you are hiding or attempting to sneak past an enemy, an NPC in the same zone will immediately detect you. Encounter checks are made with +1 die.

3-3.name: Twitchy.
3-3.description: Make an immediate supply roll for air, ammo, or power.

4-4.name: Lose Item.
4-4.description:
You lose a weapon or other important item.

Choose a relevant item, or assign a number (1–6) to each item and roll a [[1d6]] to see which is lost. In combat, you can pick up the item with a quick action.

Out of combat, you need an OBSERVATION roll and a stretch of time to find the item.

5-5.name: Indecisive.
5-5.description: Make a check on any active danger timers. If no timers are active, decide how your delay complicates the current situation.

6-6.name: Hesitant.
6-6.description: You automatically get the #10 initiative card in combat until your panic stops.

7-7.name: Freeze.
7-7.description: You’re frozen by fear, losing your next turn and unable to perform any interrupt actions before then.

8-8.name: Seek Cover.
8-8.description:
You immediately seek (full) cover in the zone, if it is cluttered.

This is an interrupt action breaking the turn order.

Once in cover, your stress level is reduced 1 step, but you lose your next turn and are unable to perform any interrupt actions before then.

If you are in an open zone, you Scream instead.

9-9.name: Scream.
9-9.description: You scream your lungs out, losing your next turn and unable to perform any interrupt actions before then. Your stress level is reduced 1 step.

10-10.name: Flee.
10-10.description:
You immediately move away from the source of panic, into any adjacent zone, if such a move is possible.

This is an interrupt action breaking the turn order. After the move, your stress level is reduced 1 step.
On your next turn and subsequent turns, you must spend all your actions to continue to move away, until you find a (reasonably) safe place, where you must remain until your panic stops. You cannot perform interrupt actions before then.

If you cannot move out of your zone, you become Catatonic (result #12) instead.

11-11.name: Frenzy.
11-11.description:
You immediately attack the nearest person or creature, friendly or not. Every friendly PC in the zone must make an immediate panic roll.

You won’t stop until you or the target is broken, or until your panic stops. You cannot perform interrupt actions before then.

12-20.name: Catatonic.
12-20.description: You’re doomed! You collapse to the floor and can’t move, rambling or staring blankly into oblivion, until your panic stops.

11-66.name: Roll on Danger Event Detail Table

.357 Magnum Revolver.name: .357 Magnum Revolver
.357 Magnum Revolver.description: A classic high calibre revolver, equally popular amongst both Frontier Marshals and lowlifes.

Armat M41A Pulse Rifle.name: Armat M41A Pulse Rifle
Armat M41A Pulse Rifle.description:
Grenade launcher.

The standard issue weapon of the USCMC, the M41A Pulse Rifle is a 10 mm automatic assault rifle with underslung 30 mm pump-action grenade launcher combined in a sturdy housing with retractable stock and optional scope. The M41A fires explosive-tip caseless standard light armor-penetrating US M309 rounds accelerated via electronic pulse. Remaining ammo is tracked via an LED counter and the rifle has two firing modes – single-shot and fully automatic. For more about the grenade launcher, see the U1.

Armat Model 37A2 12 Gauge Pump Action.name: Armat Model 37A2 12 Gauge Pump Action
Armat Model 37A2 12 Gauge Pump Action.description: A classic pump-action combat shotgun, the M37A2 is an optional weapon in use by the USCMC. Reliable and direct, the '37 is the gun you want to keep handy for close encounters.

Cutting Torch.name: Cutting Torch
Cutting Torch.description: A utilitarian blowtorch used for both welding and cutting through metal. In a pinch, a cutting torch can be used as a weapon. The Rexim EVA pistol started life as a laser cutting torch. You want to stay alive? You need to improvise.

M240 Incinerator Unit.name: M240 Incinerator Unit
M240 Incinerator Unit.description:
Fire Intensity 9.

This carbine-style flamethrower uses naphtha fuel canisters to fire a thick, steady stream of flame at a target. It is in common use by the USCMC, who deploy the weapon at the squad and fireteam level. Civilian models exist too. The troops in the field have given the M240 the unceremonious nickname of “Bake-a-Flake.” It’s a good standby weapon to have in a pinch, especially when facing off against hostile organisms. Most animals retreat from fire, yes?

Fire Effect:

If hurt, the target continues to burn with intensity 9 fire. Instead of hitting a specific target, the incinerator may be used to trigger intensity 9 fire in a zone. A single    is needed in the attack roll.

M40 HEDP Grenade.name: M40 HEDP Grenade
M40 HEDP Grenade.description:
Explosive.

Designed for the U1 grenade launcher, the High Explosive Dual Purpose M40 can also be used as a hand grenade. To use these U1 rounds as a thrown explosive, the red plastic cap must be removed and the trigger under it depressed. Three seconds later, the grenade will explode. The UPP has an equivalent made by Norcomm.

M4A3 Service Pistol.name: M4A3 Service Pistol
M4A3 Service Pistol.description: This inexpensive 9mm pistol is the standard sidearm of the USCMC. You should always have a backup for your backup, and this pistol might as well be it.

Seismic Survey Charge.name: Seismic Survey Charge
Seismic Survey Charge.description:
Explosive.

These powerful explosive charges are used to perform seismic surveys on newly colonized worlds but can also be used as weapons in a clinch.

VP-70MA6 Service Pistol.name: VP-70MA6 Service Pistol
VP-70MA6 Service Pistol.description: For nearly 70 years, the VP70 series was only found in the hands of USCMC officers from key influential military families. Over the past decade, it has begun to supplant the outdated M4A3 as the standard marine sidearm.

Watatsumi DV-303 Bolt Gun.name: Watatsumi DV-303 Bolt Gun
Watatsumi DV-303 Bolt Gun.description:
Single-shot.

The DV-303 is a construction tool that uses expanding bolts to make emergency hull repairs. The DV-303 can be turned into an improvised weapon-firing bolts like a single round shotgun- a trick first used by Frontier rebels in the early 2100's. This weapon must be reloaded (Quick Action) after each shot.

Weyland ES-4 Electrostatic Pistol.name: Weyland ES-4 Electrostatic Pistol
Weyland ES-4 Electrostatic Pistol.description:
Stun effect.

Developed a century ago, this electrostatic kinetic energy projectile weapon uses charged elements to fire high- speed armor piercing rounds. The ES-4 has a tell-tale blue muzzle-flash when fired. While a quality weapon, the pistol fell out of use before the Weyland-Yutani merger due to its cost and upkeep requirements. While it can mostly be found in use amongst high level corporate security teams from the ICSC, a select number of Colonial Marshal offices are testing out a newer model as their standard sidearm on the Frontier – along with a pair of insulator gloves.

Rexim RXF-M5A3 EVA Pistol.name: Rexim RXF-M5A3 EVA Pistol
Rexim RXF-M5A3 EVA Pistol.description: A miniaturized and weaponized version of a Weyland- Yutani laser welder in use from the 2100–2120s. This tool was originally improvised as a weapon by the J’Har rebels during the 2106 uprising on Torin Prime. Always one to find profit in anything, Weyland-Yutani studied the modifications after the war and made them the standard self-defense armament on their commercial fleet.

F44AA Pulse Rifle.name: F44AA Pulse Rifle
F44AA Pulse Rifle.description:
Unreliable.

A precursor to the modern M41A that is almost obsolete but can still be found in the hands of smugglers and colonists. It comes equipped with “aiming assist,” where a targeting sight sends data via external cable to the dynamic rifle stock which then makes minor changes to improve accuracy. It includes an LED ammo counter and folding stock. Once the service rifle of the Marines, it was prone to malfunction, and so the targeting system was subsequently redeveloped for the then upcoming M56 smart gun.

AK-4047 Pulse Assault Rifle.name: AK-4047 Pulse Assault Rifle
AK-4047 Pulse Assault Rifle.description: The UPP equivalent to the M41A Pulse Rifle, the AK-4047 is a cheap and reliable substitute. As such, the weapon often winds up in the hands of mercenaries and insurgents. While not as accurate as the M41A, the AK- 4047 is sturdier than the USCMC weapon.

M42A Scope Rifle.name: M42A Scope Rifle
M42A Scope Rifle.description: Equipped with a folding bipod, muzzle flash suppressor, and a fully adjustable stock, the M42A is the USCMC’s semi- automatic electronic pulse sniper rifle of choice. If you manage to see what’s lurking in the shadows before it sees you, you go ahead and take the shot.

Armat M41AE2 Heavy Pulse Rifle.name: Armat M41AE2 Heavy Pulse Rifle
Armat M41AE2 Heavy Pulse Rifle.description: A USCMC Squad Automatic Weapon modification of the M41A, this electric pulse support rifle has a longer barrel in place of the U1 grenade launcher. This is the machinegun you want laying down suppressing fire to cover your ass during an evac.

M56 Smart Gun.name: M56 Smart Gun
M56 Smart Gun.description:
Smart Sight.

The heavy firepower of every USCMC squad, the M56 Smartgun is mounted on an articulating arm and gimbal attached to an armored harness worn by the weapon’s operator. What makes the M56A2 a smart gun is its ability to choose targets for you. It is equipped with an infrared tracking system and data transmitter/receiver that homes in on potential threats and sends that information to a Head Mounted Sight. The M56A2 fires in either bursts or full automatic. A glancing shot can sever a limb and a full burst can cut a person in half, so watch that friendly fire, Private.

Smart Sight:

When firing the M56A2 on full auto after aiming carefully, the second and third burst of the attack will also gain the bonus for aiming.

SpaceSub ASSO-400 Harpoon Gun.name: SpaceSub ASSO-400 Harpoon Gun
SpaceSub ASSO-400 Harpoon Gun.description:
Single Shot.

Designed for aiding in emergency manual docking maneuvers, the ASSO-400 fires a grappling-hook- tipped harpoon that carries a tether. The ASSO-400 is used to close the distance between free-floating objects and personnel in space.


Harpoon Effect:

On a hit, the grappling hook attaches to the target. In zero-G, if the target is heavier than you, you can use the tether to rappel quickly toward the target (full action, moves you to Adjacent range). If you are heavier, you can instead pull the target toward you (requires a STRENGTH roll if the target resists).

Armat XM99A Phased Plasma Pulse Rifle.name: Armat XM99A Phased Plasma Pulse Rifle
Armat XM99A Phased Plasma Pulse Rifle.description:
Aim Required.

Another prototype being tested by the USCMC, the extremely potent XM99A can kill most creatures with a single shot. The weapon has a plasma charge build-up delay upon firing – so take care in lining up your target and make sure you hold steady. If you pull the trigger and check to see why it hasn’t gone off yet, you may just accidentally redefine the term “friendly fire.”

Aim Required:

This weapon must be aimed carefully (quick action) before it’s fired, giving +2 dice as normal.

M5A3 RPG Launcher.name: M5A3 RPG Launcher
M5A3 RPG Launcher.description:
Single Shot.

This shoulder-fired rocket launcher is equipped with a telescopic targeting sight.

Aim Required:

This weapon must be aimed carefully (quick action) before it’s fired.

UA 571-C Sentry Gun.name: UA 571-C Sentry Gun
UA 571-C Sentry Gun.description:
Automation.

These tripod-mounted robot sentries form an automated perimeter defense system that tracks and automatically fires upon any target that moves within range. The UA 571 series is equipped with automatic thermal and movement actuated AI targeting capabilities. The UA 571-C utilizes an M30 Autocannon. Just be mindful of your friend or foe settings before walking in front of one. Those set up with ARS – Advanced Recognition Software – can be programmed to identify friendly targets with a variable success rate. If set for motion and heat only, anything hot that moves might as well be dead.

Automation:

When activated, the Sentry Gun will fire at the closest target according to its settings with skill level 8 in RANGED COMBAT (no Agility). The attack roll can’t be pushed. The Sentry Gun can also be operated remotely by using a Head Mounted Sight.

Armat U1 Grenade Launcher.name: Armat U1 Grenade Launcher
Armat U1 Grenade Launcher.description:
Explosive.

This 30 mm pump-action is typically found as part of the M41A Pulse Rifle, but individual units do exist. When facing superior numbers, the U1 is your friend – don’t enter an alien hive without one. Well, don’t enter a hive with one, either. Just stay away from the hive. Okay?

Standard payload for the U1 is M40 High Explosive fragmentation grenades, but the launcher accommodates a variety of other grenade types from smoke grenades to electronic G2 Electroshock Grenades.

Smoke Grenade:

Causes no dam- age but blocks line of sight inside, into, and out of the target zone.

G2 Electroshock Grenades:

Causes stun damage instead of normal damage.

G2 Electroshock Grenade.name: G2 Electroshock Grenade
G2 Electroshock Grenade.description:
Explosive, Stun effect.

These grenades are called “elec- tronic ballbreakers” with good rea- son. When deployed, they propel themselves about a meter off the ground before releasing a me- ga-voltage electric pulse. The usu- ally non-lethal shock is still strong enough to freeze a person’s central nervous system. These weapons are good for crowd control. When there is only one seat left on the last shuttle to leave a space station stuck in a decaying orbit around a gas giant, pop a few of these puppies into the mob, cycle that airlock closed, and strap yourself in for the ride home.

Hand Grenade:

The stats above are for when using the G2 as a hand grenade.

Stun Baton.name: Stun Baton
Stun Baton.description:
Stun effect.

Basically a cattle prod, these electro-shock devices are designed to keep pests and livestock in order on the Frontier. While the charge isn’t strong enough to kill a human, a touch can incapacitate the target. If you see something lurking underfoot, hit it with it. Shouldn’t damage the little bastard, unless its skin is thinner than ours…

M3 Personnel Armor.name: M3 Personnel Armor
M3 Personnel Armor.description:
Built-in comm unit, PDT.

Standard issue for the USCMC, the M3 consists of a rigid armor padded vest, a flexible ballistic pad that covers the abdomen, and clamshell greaves on the lower legs. The armor protects against edged weapons and explosions, but not direct hits from high powered ammunition. It has a built-in comm unit and Personal Data Transmitter, combat webbing straps to connect a variety of equipment, and contact points which monitor the wearer’s vitals and transmit them to a tactical monitoring station.

IRC Mk.50 Compression Suit.name: IRC Mk.50 Compression Suit
IRC Mk.50 Compression Suit.description:
Vacuum protection, Comm unit, Head light, –1 to MOBILITY rolls.

State of the art when it was intro- duced six decades ago, the reliable Mk.50 Compression Suit is still a com- mon sight on the Frontier. The sturdy helmet has a comm unit and heads- up display, a lateral head light, and a wireless helmet cam that syncs to any mobile or stationary monitoring sys- tem. The suit carries a healthy supply of oxygen and maintains internal pres- sure for its wearer while in a vacuum. If you are going to get blown out into space, you want to be in a Mk.50.

Kevlar Riot Vest.name: Kevlar Riot Vest
Kevlar Riot Vest.description: A relatively lightweight vest made of woven synthetic fibers, the kevlar riot vest is the personal armor of choice for law enforcement and security details throughout the colonies.

IRC Mk.35 Pressure Suit.name: IRC Mk.35 Pressure Suit
IRC Mk.35 Pressure Suit.description:
Vacuum protection, –2 to MOBILITY rolls.

Standard issue for the USCMC, the Mk.35 is an unfortunately bulky combat pressure suit with a cumbersome recycler unit. You want to be careful wearing one of these in a fight, as the hard joints tend to seize up with extreme motion. While the inexpensive suit offers full protection from the vacuum of space, you have to spend time in a decompression chamber after spacewalking in one. Basically, this suit sucks, but if the choice is a Mk.35 or the cold of space, shut up and suit up.

Eco All-World Survival Suit.name: Eco All-World Survival Suit
Eco All-World Survival Suit.description:
Vacuum protection, Comm unit, Head light.

+2 to MOBILITY (Manual modifier) for movement in zero-G.

This EVA hardsuit has fully-articulated rotary joints and self- actuating fingers, offering a limited range of mobility, but the maximum amount of protection from the hazards of space. The helmet has a sophisticated heads-up display built in, and the suit has its own thrusters for tether-free zero-G maneuvers. The comm array on a standard Eco EVA Suit is unshielded, and thus sensitive to rogue transmissions.

Weyland-Yutani APEsuit.name: Weyland-Yutani APEsuit
Weyland-Yutani APEsuit.description:
Armor level 3 against acid, protects wearer against facehugs, SURVIVAL +2

The All Purpose Environment Suit is specialized, armored compression garb designed for combat and animal control under adverse environmental conditions. While an APEsuit cannot protect you from the vacuum of space, it does offer a limited air supply and armor, resistance to temperature extremes, and is impervious to caustic substances. The helmet includes protective eyewear and a mask to protect the wearer’s face. The suit is commonly worn by Weyland-Yutani’s security commandos and “Dog Catcher” units to contain hostile organisms, so if you see a bunch of guys show up wearing these, get the hell out of there – because what they are looking for just might find you.

P-5000 Power Loader.name: P-5000 Power Loader
P-5000 Power Loader.description:
Special Requires skill level 2 or more in HEAVY MACHINERY to be used. +3 dice to HEAVY MACHINERY and CLOSE COMBAT, base damage rating 3 in close combat attacks.

Commonly called a power loader, this mechanized exoskeleton power frame is used to transfer cargo as well as perform welding and other repairs. The exosuit amplifies your strength tenfold and is equipped with hydraulic claws for lifting and grasping.
A roll cage protects your face while you operate one, and a webbed harness keeps you strapped in in case you take a tumble. The P-5000 is difficult to master, but a pro can make operating it seem as simple as walking. Many variants exist, including a weaponized version and a wheeled work loader for larger loads.

\"Bug Juice\" Protein Drink.name: "Bug Juice" Protein Drink
\"Bug Juice\" Protein Drink.description: Commonly referred to as “bug juice,” this high protein caloric drink is made from mealworms, roaches, beetles, and other insects all raised on bug farms. Made by a large variety of manufacturers, it is a cheap and cost- effective way of keeping alive on the Frontier.

A.P.O.L.L.O..name: A.P.O.L.L.O.
A.P.O.L.L.O..description: Seegson’s answer to MU/TH/UR, A.P.O.L.L.O. was designed to coordinate Seegson’s Working Joe synthetics to run a starship. In all other regards it is less advanced than the MU/TH/UR models.

AutoDoc.name: AutoDoc
AutoDoc.description:
Effect Can give first aid (but not treat critical injuries that require surgeries) with MEDICAL AID skill level 8 (the roll cannot be pushed).

Not everyone can afford a Pauling MedPod, but almost every ship, station, and colony has at least one AutoDoc. Essentially a poor man’s version of a Pauling, the AutoDoc is an automated medical treatment device that diagnoses and treats lesser wounds and infections. It is not capable of complicated surgery, but it can reset broken bones.

Computer Terminal.name: Computer Terminal
Computer Terminal.description:
Effect - Access and process data (Comtech roll).

A computer terminal is any colony, starship, or station based electronic hardware that can access and process data via keyboard or voice commands and monitor, or hologram. Using the right codes and Comtech rolls at a terminal can potentially give you access to whatever MU/TH/UR or A.P.O.L.L.O. knows. Cost varies.

Data Transmitter Cards.name: Data Transmitter Cards
Data Transmitter Cards.description:
Effect - Transfer of audiovisual data (COMTECH +1).

Transfer of audiovisual data. DTC's are small clear plastic data transmitter cards that plug into a variety of recording equipment, such as the built-in visual and audio recorders on a space suit helmet. They wirelessly transmit data to the terminal they are synced to. Information captured by the device can be analysed by a MU/TH/UR or A.P.O.L.L.O. system or displayed on a HoloTab.

Electronic Tools.name: Electronic Tools
Electronic Tools.description:
Effect - COMTECH +1 in relevant situations.

A tool used for repairing or rewiring electronics.

HoloTab.name: HoloTab
HoloTab.description:
Effect - Strategic analysis platform (OBSERVATION and COMMAND +2).

A high-end strategic and analysis platform, a HoloTab – or Holographic Display Table – takes scanned live or recorded information fed to it and generates a three dimensional hologram of the subject. A HoloTab is usually used in conjunction with pre-existing maps or in coordination with PDTs and Parameter Uplink Spectrograph hardware.

Hydr8tion.name: Hydr8tion
Hydr8tion.description: An electrolyte solution that counteracts the dehydrating effects of hypersleep, Hydr8tion is one of the few pharmaceuticals of the space age with no side effects.

IFF Transponder.name: IFF Transponder
IFF Transponder.description:
Prevents Sentry Gun friendly fire.

A personal beacon that prevents automated sentry systems from accidently blowing friendly targets to pieces. Usually surgically implanted before a campaign, the only flaws in the system are when their signal is disrupted and when an enemy gets their hands on a transceiver for infiltration purposes. How is this accomplished if IFF's are surgically implanted? You'd be amazed what a good sharp knife can do.

M314 Motion Tracker.name: M314 Motion Tracker
M314 Motion Tracker.description: A motion-scanning device, the M314 uses high-powered ultrasonic waves to detect movement within its sensor range. Originally designed for rescue teams searching for civilians, the tracker soon found use by the military ﬁ ghting guerrilla forces in extrasolar environments.

M316 Motion Tracker.name: M316 Motion Tracker
M316 Motion Tracker.description: The drawback to the M314 is its size and weight. An experimental pulse riﬂ e mounted upgrade, the M316, is currently being ﬁ eld tested. It is compact, lightweight and easy to glance at in a ﬁ reﬁ ght. While the M316 operates about the same as the M314, it has a much more limited range. Your results may vary, but that’s what you grunts are for – cannon fodder to help the corporations ﬁ gure out how to perfect their new toys.

MU/TH/UR 6000.name: MU/TH/UR 6000
MU/TH/UR 6000.description:
Most starships, space stations, and military facilities are run via a sophisticated computer system called MU/TH/UR. Originally developed by Weyland Corporation at the end of the 21st century, the MU/TH/UR system soon became the standard for running complex automated systems and facilities. Affectionately nicknamed “Mother” by the crews who utilize these computers, over the decades various models have sported different levels of AI packages. While both the MU/TH/UR 1000 and 9000 series are sophisticated interactive models that over time can develop rudimentary personalities, most military, cargo, and utilitarian craft of today are equipped with the standard 5000 through 8000 series.
While these machines can communicate through the ship’s intercom system, most of them can only be directly accessed through the computer core. Card and punch code entry to this secure and static free chamber is only
granted to the vessel’s commanding officer. The computer core also allows the commanding officer to issue alternate commands and overrides to "Mother’s" automated routine.

MU/TH/UR 7000.name: MU/TH/UR 7000
MU/TH/UR 7000.description:
Most starships, space stations, and military facilities are run via a sophisticated computer system called MU/TH/UR. Originally developed by Weyland Corporation at the end of the 21st century, the MU/TH/UR system soon became the standard for running complex automated systems and facilities. Affectionately nicknamed “Mother” by the crews who utilize these computers, over the decades various models have sported different levels of AI packages. While both the MU/TH/UR 1000 and 9000 series are sophisticated interactive models that over time can develop rudimentary personalities, most military, cargo, and utilitarian craft of today are equipped with the standard 5000 through 8000 series.
While these machines can communicate through the ship’s intercom system, most of them can only be directly accessed through the computer core. Card and punch code entry to this secure and static free chamber is only
granted to the vessel’s commanding officer. The computer core also allows the commanding officer to issue alternate commands and overrides to "Mother’s" automated routine.

Magnetic Tape.name: Magnetic Tape
Magnetic Tape.description:
Effect - Holds up to 120 terabytes (TB) of data.

A two-hundred-year-old technology, magnetic tape cassettes have become popular on the Frontier simply because they are both disposable and cheap. Utilizing sputter deposition technology, these cassettes can hold between 60, 90, or 120 terabytes (TB) of information each. While easily disrupted by a strong magnetic pulse, the benefit of magnetic tapes is that the archaic technology that runs them produces no easily detected wave signals. Most security sensor grids are set to detect more sophisticated electronic hardware. All these factors combined have managed to keep magnetic tapes in vogue for the past fifty years.

Maintenance Jack.name: Maintenance Jack
Maintenance Jack.description:
Effect - HEAVY MACHINERY +1 in relevant situations.

A common tool used to open un- powered airlocks and divert power to or from electrical junction boxes. Can be used as a weapon (bonus +1, base damage 1).

Modular Computing Device.name: Modular Computing Device
Modular Computing Device.description:
Effect - Full audiovisual holo-graphic projector (MANIPULATION +2).

Perfected and manufactured by Weyland Corp in the 21st Century, a MCD is a high-end full audio/visual holographic projector. The holograms generated can fill a 6x6m area and are completely immersive.

Naproleve.name: Naproleve
Naproleve.description:
Effect - Reduces stress level to zero. Each dose beyond the first in the same shift gives −1 dice to all skill rolls until the end of the shift.

An injectable instant pain reliever for all strains, stresses, and irritations.

Recommended for use during any self-inflicted cesarean performed to extract an unconventional fetus from your womb.

Warning: an overdose of Naproleve can have an intoxicating effect.

Neuro Visor.name: Neuro Visor
Neuro Visor.description:
Range property: Long.

Monitor hypersleep patient. A neuro visor is a helmet with a HUD visor that allows an operator to monitor and interface with the subconscious and dreams of a subject in stasis. A skilled user (requires a Comtech roll) can also use a neurovisor to communicate with the hyper sleeping subject, and an advanced user can use one to manipulate one's dreams-so the next time you go into hypersleep, keep those dreams clean-your supervisor could be watching.

PR-PUT Uplink Terminal.name: PR-PUT Uplink Terminal
PR-PUT Uplink Terminal.description:
Effect - Remote control spacecraft (Comtech roll).

A military-grade armored and water-resistant laptop, this portable terminal has a built-in piloting joystick. With the right skills (Comtech roll) and access codes, you can use a PR-PUT to patch into a colony uplink tower and remote pilot an orbiting ship.

Pauling MedPod.name: Pauling MedPod
Pauling MedPod.description:
Effect - Can give first aid and perform surgery with MEDICAL AID skill level 12 (the roll cannot be pushed).

If you are going to get nearly dead, do it near a Pauling. The answer to space medicine, the Pauling MedPod is an autonomous medical scanner and surgical unit capable of performing bypass surgery. The Pauling MedPod can diagnose and treat infections through concentrated antibiotic injections. It can perform basic wound repair and pre-programmed surgical procedures such as an appendectomy, laparoscopic ablation and cesarean section. All models of the Pauling MedPod feature an airtight operating shield, comfortable limb restraints, a laser scalpel, computer controlled robotic surgical arms, liquid spray anesthetic and vital signs sensors, all mounted on an adjustable titanium base.

Personal Data Transmitter.name: Personal Data Transmitter
Personal Data Transmitter.description:
Effect - Monitors location and vitals (MEDICAL AID +1).

These "PDT's" transmit the recipient's location. Some models also monitor vital signs. Most corporate sponsored Frontier worlds equip their colonists with PDT's in order to keep track of them in hostile environments. PDT's can be surgically implanted, built into a pressure suit, or worn as an accessory.

Personal Medkit.name: Personal Medkit
Personal Medkit.description:
Effect - MEDICAL AID +2 for giving first aid (single use).

A Personal Medkit contains what you need to stop bleeding, disinfect a wound and cauterize it, some Pharmax bandages to wrap it up and a stim boost to keep you on your feet. A Medkit is not a permanent solution, it's more of a band aid to keep your guts from spilling out until you reach an Auto-Doc. Gives a +2 modification to Medical Aid rolls but can only be used once.

Prefab Meal.name: Prefab Meal
Prefab Meal.description:
Effect - Satisfies food needs for one day.

The average meal in space is pre-prepped flash-frozen rations. Typical meals aboard a starship include pastas, cereals, freeze-dried vegetables, stews, meatloaf and something resembling cornbread. Corporations make their employees pay for these prefab meals, despite the fact that there are few, if any, other choices and the workers are in space on company time.

Samani E-Series Watch.name: Samani E-Series Watch
Samani E-Series Watch.description:
Effect - Tracks time, oxygen, and pressure levels (Survival +1).

A dual-faced precision wristwatch, each Samani E-series device is capable of telling the time and date for two synchronized colonial locations, allowing space travellers to keep track of time back home while they are in deep space. The latest addition, the E-550, includes oxygen and pressure sensors to warn its user of a hull breach.

Seegson Microview-2000SE.name: Seegson Microview-2000SE
Seegson Microview-2000SE.description:
Extreme Range.

Location tracking. A navigational map system used on space stations, the Microview 2000SE uses the device’s coordinates aboard the station to determine that "You are Here" at all times-wherever here is at the time.

Seegson P-DAT.name: Seegson P-DAT
Seegson P-DAT.description:
Effect - Coordinate info for field teams (COMMAND +1).

Coordinate info for fields teams. A personal data tablet, a P-DAT can be synced with Spectrograph Mapping Devices, PDT's, and helmet cams to coordinate a team on the go.

Seegson System Diagnostic Device.name: Seegson System Diagnostic Device
Seegson System Diagnostic Device.description:
Effect - Troubleshoot computer systems (COMTECH +2).

The SSDD is used to troubleshoot computer and mechanical systems aboard a space station or starship. A good engineer knows how to use one of these to hack doors and computer terminals-but you didn't read that here.

Surgical Kit*.name: Surgical Kit*
Surgical Kit*.description:
Effect - MEDICAL AID +2 for first aid and surgery on critical injuries, base damage 2 if used as a weapon.

These nasty-looking instruments can mean life or death – in either the hands of a surgeon or a killer. While they are intended to save lives, in a pinch they can make for great cutting weapons.

Watatsumi DV-303 Bolt Gun*.name: Watatsumi DV-303 Bolt Gun*
Watatsumi DV-303 Bolt Gun*.description:
Effect - Ship repairs (HEAVY MACHINERY +2).

A construction tool using expanding bolts to make emergency hull repairs.

Can be used as a weapon.

Water Bottle.name: Water Bottle
Water Bottle.description:
Cost - $2– $100

Effect - Satisfies water needs for one day.

Shipboard company supplied water ($2) is rationed, cloudy, recycled, and tastes metallic, but gets you through the day. Bottles of purified water ($10) are luxury items on some worlds, and can fetch as much as $100/bottle on a barren rock.

MU/TH/UR 6500.name: MU/TH/UR 6500
MU/TH/UR 6500.description:
Most starships, space stations, and military facilities are run via a sophisticated computer system called MU/TH/UR. Originally developed by Weyland Corporation at the end of the 21st century, the MU/TH/UR system soon became the standard for running complex automated systems and facilities. Affectionately nicknamed “Mother” by the crews who utilize these computers, over the decades various models have sported different levels of AI packages. While both the MU/ TH/UR 1000 and 9000 series are sophisticated interactive models that over time can develop rudimentary personalities, most military, cargo, and utilitarian craft of today are equipped with the standard 5000 through 8000 series.
While these machines can communicate through the ship’s intercom system, most of them can only be directly accessed through the computer core. Card and punch code entry to this secure and static free chamber is only granted to the vessel’s commanding officer. The computer core also allows the commanding officer to issue alternate commands and overrides to “Mother’s” automated routine.

MU/TH/UR 9000.description:

Long-Data Disc.name: Long-Data Disc
Long-Data Disc.description:
Effect - Holds up to 10 zettabytes (ZB) of data.

After several data losses from electromagnetic pulses in the first half of the 21st century, the move was made to reintroduce and reinforce physical data storage. Weyland Corp scientists took optical disc media and enhanced it to the next level. The result is a nano-optical long-data memory disc. Called LD's, each disc can hold up to 10 zettabytes (ZB) of data. All colony and corporate records are backed up on these discs in case of an electromagnetic discharge.

Comm Unit.name: Comm Unit
Comm Unit.description: A basic radio headset for team com- munication, with a range of about 1 kilometer. A comm unit is included in several armors and environmental suits.

Seegson C-Series Magnetic Tape Recorder.name: Seegson C-Series Magnetic Tape Recorder
Seegson C-Series Magnetic Tape Recorder.description:
Effect - Record and play music (MANIPULATION +1).

An “old tech” portable audio recorder used to record or play music and audio logs. Popular models include the classic C-24 ka-boombox and the just released portable C-60 “spacewalk- man.” Now when you go EVA you can bring your country blues with you.

Flashlight.name: Flashlight
Flashlight.description:
Effect - Removes the effect of darkness in a zone.

Short Range.

Can be carried separately or attached to a ranged weapon

Parameter Uplink Spectograph Mapping Dev.name: Parameter Uplink Spectograph Mapping Device
Parameter Uplink Spectograph Mapping Dev.description:
Effect - Scans one zone per stretch in stealth mode, automatically detects enemies unless hidden.

Sometimes called “Pups,” these cost-prohibitive mapping devices have been in use for a good hundred years. Pups employ limited anti- gravity propulsion to float through, across, and over otherwise difficult to navigate terrain. As these orbs scout about, they constantly scan a 360-degree area around the device with mapping lasers. The Pups then send the spectrograph information back to a synced device, usually a starship or ground-based HoloTab or a mon- itoring station in a mobile command vehicle. They can also detect life- forms, atmospheric conditions, tox- ins, and more. Pups were given their nickname because they emit a haunting, hound- like howling sound as they seek and scan.

Mechanical Cutting Torch*.name: Mechanical Cutting Torch*
Mechanical Cutting Torch*.description:
Effect - Construction and repairs (HEAVY MACHINERY +2).

A utilitarian blowtorch used for both welding and cutting through metal. Can be used as a weapon.

Power Cell.name: Power Cell
Power Cell.description:
Effect - Restores full power supply to one item.

Needed to recharge motion trackers and other electric gear.

Neversleep Pills.name: Neversleep Pills
Neversleep Pills.description:
Effect - Stress level +1 but removes the need for sleep for a day, during which you cannot relieve stress.

Fast-acting supplement that keeps you going well past your bedtime.

Excessive use can cause stroke or heart attack.

Candy Bar.name: Candy Bar
Candy Bar.description:
Effect - Satisfies food needs for one day.

Luxury items on the Frontier, these guilty pleasures can give you a sugar rush if you need it

Coffee.name: Coffee
Coffee.description:
Effect - Stress level +1 and postpones fatigue from lack of sleep for one shift. Additional doses in the same shift have no effect.

Coffee is supplied on most company ships and stations free of charge for the crew. Grown in Guatemala on Earth, Weyland-Yutani coffee is the highest rated in the territories, and free coffee is considered one of the perks of W-Y employment. If you are on the verge of dozing off, coffee can give you a caffeine boost to get you through the morning.

Colony Specialty Meals.name: Colony Specialty Meals
Colony Specialty Meals.description:
Cost - $20–$300

Effect - Satisfies food needs for one day, stress level –1.

Planetside colony grub can be a better thing, as colonists get creative with their rations to create new "culinary delights." Some colonies grow their own livestock while others have access to edible indigenous wildlife, creating a wide variety of cuisine ranging from Terraform 3's bovine burgers and steaks to boiled Tanakan scorpion thorax to kelp salad and sushi from Bracken's World. Increases your Food Supply and reduces Stress Level one step. Costs between $20-$300

Damage reduced over range.

Sensor Drones.description: SENSOR DRONES: When launched, sensor drones create false sensor signatures that can maneuver at speed and can lure away incoming missiles and railgun targeting systems.

Tactical Nuke.name: Tactical Nuke
Tactical Nuke.description:
Missile cost: $1,000,000

TACTICAL NUKES: Shipborne nukes are deployed from orbit to destroy planetary based targets, even entire colonies. A 50-megaton nuke will completely destroy all buildings and kill all living beings within a 10 km radius, and cause damage to buildings and people up to 100 km away from the center of detonation. In addition, a high-altitude detonation will create an electromagnetic pulse that destroys unshielded electronics. A nuclear missile battery can typically fit five missiles. Individual missiles must be purchased separately.

Added Hardpoint, size II.name: Added Hardpoint, size II
Added Hardpoint, size II.description: ADDED HARDPOINTS: You add one more hardpoint to your ship, of the same size as your current biggest hardpoint or smaller. This upgrade can be purchased twice.

Added Hardpoint, size III.name: Added Hardpoint, size III
Added Hardpoint, size III.description: ADDED HARDPOINTS: You add one more hardpoint to your ship, of the same size as your current biggest hardpoint or smaller. This upgrade can be purchased twice.

Air Scrubbers I.name: Air Scrubbers I
Air Scrubbers I.description: AIR SCRUBBERS: Machinery needed to supply the crew with breathable air. Carbon filters clean pollutants from the air while churning machines elec- trolyze the water and generate oxygen. Air scrubbers come in many sizes and price levels, depending on how many people they need to keep supplied.
